III. 
The SITP’s CAPEX, OPEX, and RTB Adjustments
5 
Q.
Please describe the SITP’s proposed adjustment to the Companies’ 
6 
CAPEX budget. 
7 
A.
The SITP recommends a forecasting adjustment that includes the removal 
8 
of 30 projects from the Companies’ CAPEX budget. After adjusting for 
9 
the proposed removal from the Rate Year IT&D CAPEX forecast, the 
10 
Service Company’s IT&D CAPEX forecast would be reduced by 62.60 
11 
percent, from $307.922 million to $115.115 million.    
12 
13 
Q.
Please describe the SITP’s proposed adjustment to the Companies’ 
14 
OPEX and RTB levels.  
15 
A.
As a result of the SITP’s proposed removal of 30 projects from the 
16 
Companies’ CAPEX budget, the Service Company OPEX and RTB 
17 
levels would be reduced by the SITP by $43.031 million and $14.713 
18 
million, respectively, in FY 2025. 
19 
20 


--- Page 9 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of the Information Technology & Digital Panel 
Page 7 of 29 
Q.
Did the SITP explain why it believes that the Companies could meet
1 
their legal obligations with a CAPEX budget of $115.115 million?
2 
A.
No.  The SITP never explains why it believes that the Companies could
3 
continue to operate effectively with an annual CAPEX budget of only
4 
$115.115 million when IT&D actual CAPEX has exceeded that in each of
5 
the last five fiscal years.
6 
7 
Q.
What was the IT&D CAPEX amount reflected in the Companies’ 
8 
rates during the FY 2021 to FY 2023 period? 
9 
A.
The Companies’ rate allowance for IT&D CAPEX was $225 million in 
10 
FY 2021 and $150 million in each of FY 2022 and FY 2023. 
11 
12 
Q.
What is the significance of this information? 
13 
A.
The fact that the Companies invested $261.379 million and $307.906 
14 
million in FY 2022 and FY 2023, respectively, compared to a rate 
15 
allowance of $150 million in each of these years demonstrates that a much 
16 
larger level of IT&D investment was deemed necessary for the Companies 
17 
to fulfill their service obligations.  The Companies’ need to invest between 
18 
$111.379 million and $157.906 million in IT&D systems that were not 
19 
compensated in rates provides compelling evidence that the Companies 
20 


--- Page 10 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of the Information Technology & Digital Panel 
Page 8 of 29 
cannot possibly manage their systems under the $115.115 million IT&D 
1 
CAPEX budget recommended by the SITP. 
2 
3 
Q.
What would the likely consequences be if the Commission were to set 
4 
rates reflecting the SITP’s recommended level of IT-related CAPEX? 
5 
A.
Setting rates that reflected the SITP’s proposed amount of IT&D CAPEX 
6 
in the Rate Year would severely compromise the Companies’ ability to 
7 
continue to provide safe and reliable service.  The SITP’s recommended 
8 
budget would prevent the Companies’ from advancing strategic IT&D 
9 
projects as it would require them to solely focus capital spending on 
10 
maintaining existing core systems.  Of particular concern, removing the 
11 
C2C Enhancements project, the Physical Security and Cybersecurity 
12 
projects (consisting of Identity and Access Management, Network 
13 
Security Program, Operational Technical Security, Security Orchestration 
14 
Automation and Response (“SOAR”), and Security Vulnerability 
15 
Management Program), the Digital Platforms and Infrastructure 
16 
Technology (“DPIT”) Networks investments, and the Backoffice Refresh 
17 
project create undue risks to the Companies’ ability to provide safe, 
18 
reliable service.  The SITP’s removal of these high-value investments will 
19 
restrict the Companies’ ability to make necessary enhancements to its 
20 
customer information system after completing KEDNY’s conversion to 
21 


--- Page 11 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of the Information Technology & Digital Panel 
Page 9 of 29 
 
CSS and compromise the Companies’ ability to address security risks to 
1 
its physical infrastructure and information systems with investments that 
2 
are a continuation of existing in-flight initiatives.   
3 
 
4 
IT&D investments provide the critical backbone to every other function in 
5 
the Companies, whether it be customer-facing services, critical 
6 
infrastructure assets, or day-to-day operations.  These projects are 
7 
essential to the Companies’ efforts to strengthen physical and digital 
8 
assets, enhance customer information systems, and maintain the IT&D 
9 
systems that enable all other systems to operate.  The maintenance of the 
10 
Companies’ IT&D systems is absolutely critical to the Companies’ ability 
11 
to safely and reliably serve customers now and in the future.  Adoption of 
12 
SITP’s IT&D CAPEX budget for ratemaking purposes would not provide 
13 
sufficient funds to permit the Companies to successfully manage their 
14 
IT&D functions.

Q. 
The SITP (at 63-64) states that it is concerned about the Service 
1 
Company’s ability to meet its budgets and states that if the 
2 
Commission rejects the SITP’s project-by-project cuts then it should 
3 
consider applying an adjustment to reflect the Companies’ historic 
4 
underspending.  Do you have any comments concerning this 
5 
recommendation? 
6 
A. 
Yes.  As shown on the SITP’s Exhibit __ (SITP-5), over the period of the 
7 
current rate plans, FY 2021 through FY 2023, the combined KEDLI and 
8 
KEDNY average of CAPEX spending for core IT projects was $267.179 
9 
million, only 0.6 percent below the average CAPEX budget of $268.675 
10 
million.  The five-year average of IT&D CAPEX core IT spending during 
11 
the period FY 2019 to FY 2023 was $214.559 million, only 1.3 percent 
12 
below the average CAPEX budget of $217.333 million.  These modest 
13 
budget variances completely refute the justification for the SITP’s 
14 
recommended disallowance of nearly 62 percent of the Companies’ Rate 
15 
Year CAPEX budget.   
16 
 
17 
Due to the nature of IT&D projects, it is not unusual for projects to be 
18 
delayed or accelerated to meet the needs of rapidly changing businesses.  
19 
The Companies face considerable challenges every year in meeting and 
20 
managing their IT&D budgets.  The Joint Proposal adopted in the 2019 
21 


--- Page 13 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of the Information Technology & Digital Panel 
Page 11 of 29 
 
KEDNY and KEDLI Rate Cases recognizes this challenge by requiring 
1 
the Companies to reconcile their IT&D spending in the aggregate, not at 
2 
the individual project level.  Despite the challenges involved in managing 
3 
an IT&D budget, the Companies’ budget versus actual CAPEX spending 
4 
over the term of the current rate plans reflects an underspending of only 
5 
0.6 percent.  Given this performance, it is difficult for the Panel to 
6 
understand why the SITP believes it is reasonable to reduce the 
7 
Companies’ forecast Rate Year CAPEX budget by nearly 62 percent, or 
8 
over $190 million.  It is inconceivable that the Companies will have a 
9 
budget shortfall of anything approaching that amount.  From the 
10 
Companies’ perspective, the Companies’ recent performance in managing 
11 
their IT&D CAPEX budget would not support any adjustment greater than 
12 
the 1.3 percent budget variance experienced over the last 5 years. 
13

Q. 
Do the Companies agree with the SITP (at 24) that the risk of 
11 
overspending a budget identified in an Investment Estimation Tool 
12 
(“IET”) is a reasonable basis for the SITP to remove a project from 
13 
the IT&D CAPEX forecast?  
14 
A. 
No.  While early-stage cost estimates included in the IET generally allow 
15 
for a greater variance than at the time of sanctioning, the Companies are 
16 
subject to a downward-only reconciliation mechanism for Service 
17 
Company Rents, Net Utility Plant, and Depreciation that shields customers 
18 
from any overspending above the IT&D revenue requirement approved by 
19 
the Commission.  The reconciliation mechanism also prevents the 
20 
Companies from recovering more than the revenue requirement when the 
21 


--- Page 15 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of the Information Technology & Digital Panel 
Page 13 of 29 
 
Companies spend less than what was initially budgeted.  As a result, the 
1 
risk associated with overspending is wholly borne by the Company.  
2 
 
3 
Q. 
Do the Companies and Staff agree with continuing the downward-
4 
only reconciliation mechanism proposed by Staff (at 67)? 
5 
A. 
Yes, the Companies and Staff agree that the downward-only reconciliation 
6 
mechanism should remain in effect.  
7 
 
8 
Q.  
The SITP asserts (at 15) that IETs do not provide enough information 
9 
to substantiate moving forward with multi-million dollar IT&D 
10 
investments.  Do you agree?  
11 
A.  
No.  In the Companies’ responses to IR Nos. DPS-457 and DPS-457 
12 
Supplemental, which Staff included in Exhibit ___ (SITP-1), IETs were 
13 
provided for all projects not-yet-sanctioned.  The IETs provide key 
14 
attributes of proposed future investments, including investment 
15 
descriptions, cost estimates, scope, timing, and the expected benefiting 
16 
operating company, among other details.  While prepared when a project 
17 
is in conceptual development, a range of criteria are evaluated including 
18 
risks to achieve, CAPEX, OPEX, and RTB cost considerations, 
19 
alternatives, and benefits to ensure that IT&D projects that reach the 
20 
sanctioning stage have been vetted for overall success with the 
21 


--- Page 16 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of the Information Technology & Digital Panel 
Page 14 of 29 
 
information available to the project team at the outset.  IETs are developed 
1 
with input from project manager experience, historical cost trends, and 
2 
labor, hardware, software, and other anticipated expenses. Further, IT&D 
3 
projects that continue to advance after an IET is prepared are still required 
4 
to complete both partial and full sanctioning before progressing to the 
5 
start-up phase.   
6 
 
7 
Q. 
Are the IETs provided in this case consistent with the information 
8 
that is utilized by National Grid to develop its IT&D CAPEX budgets 
9 
each year? 
10 
A. 
Yes.  Due to the nature of IT&D projects and the Companies’ rapidly 
11 
changing business and information technology environments, National 
12 
Grid’s IT&D CAPEX budget for any given year will include projects that 
13 
are in the start-up phase and for which only IETs have been developed, 
14 
projects that have been partially sanctioned, and projects that have been 
15 
fully sanctioned.  To manage its business efficiently and effectively, 
16 
National Grid must develop a budget that includes the IT&D CAPEX 
17 
projects that need to be placed in service in a given year, as well as multi-
18 
year investments still under development.  Because the IT&D budget 
19 
serves as the foundation for the Companies’ rate filings (which, in New 
20 
York, utilize a fully forecast rate year), it is unavoidable that a significant 
21 


--- Page 17 ---
Rebuttal Testimony of the Information Technology & Digital Panel 
Page 15 of 29 
 
number of projects included in the Rate Year forecast will be in the IET 
1 
phase, or only partially sanctioned for prior fiscal years.  Additionally, the 
2 
IT&D strategic business plan is developed annually, with a ten-year 
3 
horizon, and is informed by and inclusive of forecast cost estimates 
4 
contained in project specific IETs.  Clearly, IETs are a necessary and 
5 
proper part of a successfully functioning budget process and the costs 
6 
estimates reflected in IETs should be reflected in budgets that form the 
7 
basis of reasonable utility rates.

Report on 
National Grid’s Information Technology Reporting Format 
 
I. 
Background 
 
 
Pursuant to Section IV.6.5 of the Joint Proposal approved by the New York State Public 
Service Commission (“Commission”) on August 12, 2021 in Case 19-G-0309 et al.,1 The 
Brooklyn Union Gas Company d/b/a National Grid NY (“KEDNY”) and KeySpan Gas East 
Corporation d/b/a National Grid (“KEDLI”) (together “National Grid” or “the Companies”) 
submit this Report on National Grid’s Quarterly and Annual Information Technology Reporting 
Format (“Report”).  The Joint Proposal provides that the Companies are to collaborate with 
Department of Public Service Staff (“Staff”) to modify and improve upon the format of quarterly 
and annual information technology (“IT”) reporting Staff currently receives from the 
Companies’ Upstate New York affiliate.2  The Joint Proposal further requires that the Companies 
file a report with the Commission Secretary no later than 90 days prior to the start of Rate Year 
Three of the rate plan describing the reporting requirements agreed to through the collaborative 
process between Staff and the Companies.3  This Report describes the Companies’ planned 
reporting format in accordance with the requirements in Section IV.6.5 of the Joint Proposal. 
 
II. 
Joint Proposal Requirements 
 
 
The Joint Proposal sets forth general requirements for quarterly and annual IT investment 
reporting by the Companies.  Among the goals for a modified reporting format are to enable 
easier monitoring and understanding by Staff of individual IT project status and progress, as well 
as providing a clear view of the entire IT investment portfolio.  This would include greater 
transparency of the Companies’ IT investments, sanctioning, budgeting and approval process, 
while “avoiding placing an undue burden on both the Companies to compile the information and 
on Staff to review the information.”4  The Joint Proposal provides that the modified reporting 
format should streamline quarterly reporting to present strategic, executive-level information on 
IT project status to make it easier to monitor project status and progress in terms of schedule, 
scope, and budget for each of the investment categories (as well as for individual projects within 
each category) and for major IT projects (e.g., transformation investments, such as Gas Business 
 
1 Case 19-G-0309, Proceeding on Motion of the Commission as to the Rates, Charges, Rules and Regulations of The 
Brooklyn Union Gas Company d/b/a National Grid NY for Gas Service, Case 19-G-0310, Proceeding on Motion of 
the Commission as to the Rates, Charges, Rules and Regulations of KeySpan Gas East Corporation d/b/a National 
Grid for Gas Service, and Case 18-M-0270 Petition for Approval Pursuant to Public Service Law Section 113(2), of 
a Proposed Allocation of Certain Tax Refunds Between KeySpan Gas East Corporation d/b/a National Grid and 
Ratepayers, Order Approving Joint Proposal as Modified, and Imposing Additional Requirements (issued and 
effective August 12, 2021).  Hereinafter, the Joint Proposal approved in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-0310 is referred 
to as the “Joint Proposal.”   
2 Staff currently receives quarterly and annual IT reports from Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation d/b/a National 
Grid (“Niagara Mohawk”) pursuant a requirement from Niagara Mohawk’s most recently approved rate case. See 
Cases 17-E-0238 and 17-G-0239, Proceeding on Motion of the Commission as to the Rates, Charges, Rules and 
Regulations of Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation d/b/a National Grid for Electric and Gas Service, Order 
Adopting Terms of Joint Proposal and Establishing Electric and Gas Rate Plans (issued and effective March 15,

2 
 
Enablement, Advanced Metering Infrastructure, Customer Information System, etc.).  For 
quarterly IT reports, the modified format should, at a minimum: 
 Identify project issues and risks 
 Identify project milestones 
 Provide details on project governance for each of the individual projects.  
For the annual IT reports, in addition to the requirements of the quarterly reports, the Companies 
should provide more detailed descriptions of the status of projects, expanding as necessary to 
address any issues identified.  
 
Because the IT portfolio is managed at the National Grid USA Service Company level for 
the benefit of all the US operating companies, IT reporting is to be consistent across all New 
York jurisdictions and show the full IT portfolio.  In addition, variance reporting (including root 
cause determination of variances and corrective actions), allocations to each company, and status 
of savings associated with retirement of legacy systems being replaced by new IT investments 
would continue to be included. 
 
III. 
Current Reporting Format 
 
The current IT quarterly report provides an explanation of the top ten projects by annual 
budget in the following investment categories:    
(1) Regulatory, Legal and Compliance Mandates.  
(2) Business Programs and Projects. 
(3) Technology/Infrastructure Foundation and Reliability.   
 
For any of the top ten projects in the foregoing categories with a budget-versus-actual variance 
greater than 10 percent, the report provides an explanation of the reason for the variance.  The 
quarterly report also provides a listing of all projects delivered in that quarter, all projects 
discontinued, all new demand, and a budget exception report. 
 
The final report of the year is the annual report,  In addition to the information included 
in the quarterly reports, the annual report format currently includes a listing of all projects 
delivered in the fiscal year, and also is accompanied by the sanction papers for all approved 
projects over $1 million. 
 
IV. 
Collaboration with Staff and Planned Reporting Format 
 
On October 13, 2021, the Companies met with Staff to review the status of the 
Companies’ IT investment program, and to discuss a proposed modified format of the periodic 
IT investment reports.  At that meeting, Staff provided feedback on the Companies’ proposed 
quarterly and annual IT reporting formats.  Based on that feedback, the Companies plan to 
format future IT investment reports as follows.  
 
First, the Companies intend to provide their Annual IT Investment Plan at the beginning 
of each fiscal year as is currently the practice with Niagara Mohawk.  This Annual IT Investment 
Plan provides a list of proposed IT investments with associated budgets and planned in service 
dates for the forthcoming year.   
Exhibit __ (ITDP-1R) 
Page 3 of 15


--- Page 37 ---
3 
As discussed at the October 13 meeting, the current quarterly and annual reporting format 
is very segmented and detailed but does not provide Staff much insight as to how National Grid 
is delivering the IT Strategy.  The Companies therefore plan to modify the report format to 
include information in the format used in National Grid’s internal IT management reporting to 
provide Staff with the same level of insight provided to senior IT management.  The proposed 
reporting would be at the portfolio level spanning six separate areas of IT: 
1)
Security
2)
Information and Operations
3)
Customer
4)
Group Functions
5)
Gas
6)
Electric
Each report would include the following information for each portfolio: 

Financial Section – Financial Summary, Details of Opex & Capex Spend for the portfolio
as a whole, a financial forecast.

Project Delivery Section – A commentary with Key Challenges, a Mobilization Summary
as to totals of completed, inflight and pipeline projects, a Delivery Methodology
summary.

Priority Programs Summary – Status of the programs, Red/Amber/Green status, and
Budget.
Included in Attachment 1 is the planned format of the quarterly IT report.  The modified format 
is intended to address concerned voiced by Staff regarding the level of detail being provided in 
the IT portfolio reports.  The Power Business Intelligence report for each IT portfolio comparing 
actual-versus-budget for the fiscal year to date, together with a year-end forecast-versus-budget, 
is intended to provide the necessary detail for Staff to effectively evaluate the status of National 
Grid’s IT investment program.  Information from the portfolio report will provide the strategic 
insight, and the individual project detail from the Power Business Intelligence report will enable 
a complete picture of project performance. 
The Companies will continue to provide a list of all projects placed into service by fiscal 
year end.  However, the Companies are proposing not to send the large volume of sanction 
papers that have been sent in the past.  Rather, the Companies think it would be more efficient to 
send only those papers specifically requested by Staff.  At this stage, the Companies also are not 
proposing to include a Budget Exception Report, or a listing of projects placed in service at each 
quarter end.    
V.
Next Steps
The Companies plan to file their first quarterly IT report using the modified format within 
sixty days of the end of the third quarter of FY 2022 (December 31, 2021).  The Companies 
expect to continue to coordinate with, and take feedback from, Staff in the future to further 
evolve the report format to achieve a product that is easy for Staff to use to better understand the 
Companies’ IT capital investments and that is not unduly burdensome for National Grid to 
produce.

Executive Summary - Customer
Financial Summary
Priority Programs
To achieve Customer's North Star vision of improving customer engagement and reducing the cost to serve we are taking a 
“Digital first” approach. This means (i) improving the customer-facing systems to drive up self-service (ii) reengineering back 
office processes to generate internal efficiencies (iii) Addressing the legacy technology that limit our speed to value (iv) and
building a data layer that provides real-time information to both customers and customer service representatives.

National Grid 
| IT & Digital Portfolio Review & Status Update | September 21
Executive Summary - GBU
Financial Summary
Priority Programs
The IT US Gas and Capital Delivery portfolio is aligned to the strategic focus areas of the Gas Business through thematic strategic programs like Gas Business Enablement 
to support the transformation of the future gas business and execution of tactical initiatives that are tied to shorter term business goals. The business outcomes for these 
programs and projects focus on: Implementing capabilities not previously available to Gas, Improving E2E capital efficiency while improving safety and reliability, Delivery of 
field performance in efficiency, safety, compliance, and customer satisfaction, Implementing standardized processes, tools & technologies, Standardize work practices and 
processes in the field using enterprise-wide systems and technologies.
FY22 Budget was approved for 14 projects out of 17 proposed. 2 of the approved projects will be delayed/differed to later in FY22 or FY23 due to business changes. Budget 
allotted to those projects is being reallocated to PIF, NSRMS(New Storms) and DR(Demand Response) projects which will provide value to the busines(See financial 
overview)

Executive Summary - EBU
Priority Programs
•
RI Divestiture: The January 1st Day 1 planning date has been updated based upon the agreed upon procedural schedule.
The planned date for 
regulatory approval is February 25, 2022, which would lead to a Day 1 cutover in early March. All streams currently on track for Day 1 following 
closure of key Finance, HR and Supply Chain decisions. 
•
GIS Phase 1 Go-Live:  Successfully completed on September 6th , which enables new types of equipment such as Electric Vehicle Charging 
Stations, Energy Storage, Inverters and Substation Equipment to be available for use in GIS, and interface downstream systems/processes
•
Active Resource Integration (ARI): Product received approval from electric leadership at the August 30th Digital Change Board Meeting to move 
forward; validation work expected to start on 11/1.
•
Discussions underway with Business around Digital initiatives (ICU Out and GridMD) slated for FY22 yet are still pending approval from the 
Digital Change Board.
•
Network & Telecom IT/OT Operating Model, Transformation Roadmap and Savings Opportunities Analysis on target to be delivered in October

National Grid 
Power BI Reports
The following are samples of Power BI reports National Grid has developed.   The next four pages illustrate the type 
of information the Companies can provide from a total portfolio perspective down to individual project performance. 
The report would provide an overall portfolio review of year-to-date performance to budget and year-end forecast to 
budget for each portfolio similar to what appears on page 8.  A portfolio view with information similar to that shown 
on page 9 would also be provided.  
Budget versus actual view for each project would be provided as shown on page 10.
Finally, the report would include each project’s actual and forecasted spend profile similar to that shown on page 11.
Although there would be numerous pages the Companies can readily automate production and provide a consistent 
report.  The Power BI reports would provide a comprehensive and transparent presentation of the IT program from 
the portfolio level down to individual project level and enable review down to an appropriate level of detail to be able 
to understand overall performance and identify areas of concern.

I. 
Introduction 
 
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submit this Information Technology (“IT”) Capital Investment Quarterly Report 
(“IT Quarterly Report”) for the third quarter of fiscal year 2022 (“FY22”).1  Pursuant to the Public 
Service Commission’s (“Commission”) January 20, 2022 Order in Cases 20-E-0380 20-G-0381, 
and August 12, 2021 Order in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-0310, the Company is to provide 
quarterly variance reports to Department of Public Service Staff (“Staff”) regarding IT capital 
projects and investments.2  The IT Quarterly Report provides an explanation of the Company’s 
overall IT investment plan approach; descriptions of program investment categories; and a 
comparison of budgeted to actual spending. 
 
IT capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s operating 
companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. (“Service 
Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara Mohawk, 
KEDNY and KEDLI in the form of Service Company rent expense once the investments are in-
service.  The Service Company rent expense includes a return on the capital investment (net of 
deferred taxes) plus booked depreciation expense. 
 
Through Q3 FY22, National Grid spent $183.0 million compared to a year-to-date Service 
Company budget of $228.1 million, representing a $45.1 million underspend.  Attachment 1 
includes detail on budgets and actual spending for each of the portfolios and commentary regarding 
performance which has been presented to each of the Chief Information Officers responsible for 
the respective portfolios.  
 
Attachment 2 includes a detailed breakdown of individual project spend by portfolio compared to 
the budgeted spend for each of those projects. 
 
II. 
Program Categories/Spending Rationales 
 
National Grid has re-organized the US Information Technology organization into six areas:

IT capital investment also is tracked based on these area designations. Descriptions of each 
portfolio category/spending rationale are provided below. 
 
Group Functions  
Group Functions executes National Grid’s digital roadmaps, leveraging technology and 
reimagining processes in support of Finance, Enterprise Business Services, Human Resources, 
Legal, and Safety Health & Environmental, continuing to upgrade SOX related systems, and 
retiring outdated systems. 
 
United States Electric 
Provides IT Support to our US Electric Distribution and Transmission businesses.  Modernizing 
our key legacy operational systems while building capabilities that will effectively enable the 
energy transition and transformation to a Distribution System Operator (DSO).   Through digital 
delivery, the Electric CIO organization provides greater efficiency and data driven insights into 
our workforce operations:  
 More automated and reliable grid controls systems  
 Capital programs and projects that support the proliferation of Distributed Energy 
Resources (DERs)  
 A growing market of prosumer electric customers 
 
United States Gas 
Provides IT Support to our US Gas Distribution and Transmission businesses developing digital 
products based on the foundation of gas business enablement, that deliver continuous improvement 
of our asset lifecycle management capabilities through:   
 Risk based asset investment planning  
 Performance based maintenance  
 AI based work optimization  
 Mobile field products 
 
Customer 
Provides IT Support to our US Customer business, delivering best-in-class digital products that 
increase engagement and reduce cost to serve:  
 Modernizing our legacy “back-end” IT estate to support more digital products  
 Liberating data and creating an abstracted and real-time customer data platform to assist 
with achieving energy efficiency ambitions  
 
Infrastructure and Operations (“I&O”) 
Supports our internal IT Architecture covering Cloud and Hosting, Critical Network Infrastructure, 
Networks, End User Experience and Operations.  I&O is focused on reducing National Grid’s 
Exhibit ___ (ITDP-2R) 
Page 3 of 303


--- Page 53 ---
Page 3 of 4 
 
 
technical debt through cost effective, modernized IT infrastructure enabling cloud capabilities that 
meet our risk profile.   The organization enables a connected, seamless enterprise that is flexible, 
secure, reliable and scalable while maintaining acceptable levels of technical debt and risk. 
 
Security 
The Security function protects our people, premises, and digital systems with the objective of 
maintaining trust in National Grid services, focusing on: 
 Reduction in likelihood and impact of security incidents 
 Compliance with relevant laws, standards and regulations (e.g., NERC, PCI DSS, GDPR, 
NIS-R) 
 Improved user experience and standard of security practices across National Grid 
 
The Security function aims to reduce the likelihood and impact of physical and cyber security 
incidents affecting National Grid. It does this by championing security best practices, technology 
and promoting a security-awareness culture.

for each of the portfolios: Group Functions; US Electric, US Gas, Customer, I&O and 
Security.   Each portfolio consists of 3 pages: 
a. The first page provides a narrative financial and business overview.   The three 
charts on this page show: operating expenses, capital expenses, and total 
expenses; FY22 actuals and forecast by period versus budget, with trend lines 
showing prior year expenditure and run rate.   This page also shows the full year 
total expenditure budget and forecast and the Q3 actual total expenditure 
compared to the Q3 budget. 
b. The second page of the portfolio sections has two charts on the top left of the 
page: the top chart is actual expenditure versus budget by program year to date.  
The second chart compares full fiscal year forecast versus annual budget by 
program.  A priority investments list for the portfolio and their status appears at 
the top right hand of the page.   Blue means complete, green means on track, 
amber means some risk, and red means focused intervention required. On the 
bottom half of this page is a chart showing actual and forecasted spend for FY22

compared to budget, prior year and FY22 for the portfolio.   Each bar is color-

c. The third page of each portfolio section provides a status update on the various

B. Attachment 2 
 
INVP Level Variances - This attachment provides a detailed listing of individual projects 
in each of the six portfolios.  Actual spend to date is provided, together with the budgeted 
allowance and the year-to-date variance.  A monthly forecast walk also is provided to give 
the year-end forecast, with a comparison to year-end budget and corresponding variance. 
 
In addition to detailing each of the six portfolios, Attachment 2 also includes a section for 
“Other” costs.  The “Other” category has three elements:  
 The IT4IT sub-category.  This is essentially a funding source for net present value 
positive projects to enable efficiency savings in National Grid’s IT run-the-business 
operations.    
 The “other” sub-category is the allocation of overheads such as Enterprise 
Architecture and Solution Delivery operating expenses to a centralized account.  
The capital charges for this overhead are made directly to individual projects. 
 Finally, the burdens are the net removal of operating expense burdens to ensure IT 
reporting agrees to Corporate Controllable Cost reporting.

In FY22, Electric IT focused on -
1)
reducing operational risk by upgrading / replacing end of life systems, e.g., Energy accounting system migration to Wholesale Settlement application, US Control-Transmission Outage Application (iTOA)

reimagining ways of working for people in field, for investment planners etc.
•
Vegetation Management Optimization: implemented MVP allowing for optimizing cycle prune and hazard tree removal plans. VMO MVP is expected to drive ~$2M in Type 1 Opex Contractor Costs in FY22. ,
•
OnMyWay - digitization of Confirming Work Request (CWR) forms for people in field; crews in NY and NE completed a total of 50,000+ jobs using the OMW app in the first 10 months of deployment, Benefits 
in FY22 are expected to be:  Type 1: ~$3M Capex / ~$0.5M Opex  ; Type 2: ~$1.5M Capex / ~$0.5M Opex 
•

reduced cost.  FutureNow MVP Roll Out on 2/14/22, which will help drive the following savings in FY23 through its workplan optimization capabilities:  Type 1: ~$10M Capex / ~$1.5M Opex

National Grid 
Executive Summary – Customer
Financial Summary
Budget ($M)
51.5
Forecast ($M)
57.5
YTD Actual ($M)
41.5
Totex
Customer is making significant strides in digital enablement and improving the customer experience. Two advancements of note are the delivery of a unified web portal 
to NYC Gas customers in November integration of contact center third party vendors onto the AIMS (IVR suite) to provide a seamless call experience to customers. The 
User Experience scores have increased significantly (over 20 points) for NYC Gas customers since the migration to the new web platform, however due to stability 
problems we have put on hold deploying to UNY and LI.
The portfolio is on target to utilize the full budget for 
delivery.
In Q4 we will see the run rate of Customer Data 
Platform increase as the team matures and 
additional resources come on board.  We also have 
two new mandate and compliance efforts kicking off 
in Q4. 
The largest variance is in the Unified Web Portal 
(UWP) effort. Leading up to the UWP launch in 
November and since, we have had persistent 
stability issues due to multiple root causes including  
bad data; missing or incorrect user profiles; 
software errors; and poorly tuned servers. There is 
an active war room to address the issues  We have 
made progress with daily incidents reducing from 
103 to 37.  The additional resources required to 
stabilize the experience is the primary driver of 
additional costs. The UWP project will continue to 
run over budget into early FY23 as the stability 
problems are addressed.
.

Information Technology Capital Investment Report for  
Quarter Ended March 31, 2022 
 
 
I. 
Introduction 
 
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submit this Information Technology (“IT”) Capital Investment Quarterly Report 
(“IT Quarterly Report”) for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2022 (“FY22”).1  Pursuant to the Public 
Service Commission’s (“Commission”) January 20, 2022 Order in Cases 20-E-0380 and 20-G-
0381, and August 12, 2021 Order in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-0310, the Company is to provide 
quarterly variance reports to Department of Public Service Staff (“Staff”) regarding IT capital 
projects and investments.2  The IT Quarterly Report provides an explanation of the Company’s 
overall IT investment plan approach; descriptions of program investment categories; and a 
comparison of budgeted to actual spending. 
 
IT capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s operating 
companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. (“Service 
Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara Mohawk, 
KEDNY and KEDLI, in the form of Service Company rent expense once the investments are in-
service.  The Service Company rent expense includes a return on the capital investment (net of 
deferred taxes) plus booked depreciation expense. 
 
Through Q4 FY22, National Grid spent $299.1 million compared to a year-to-date Service 
Company budget of $328.3 million, representing a $29.2 million underspend.  Attachment 1 
includes detail on budgets and actual spending for each of the portfolios and commentary regarding 
performance which has been presented to each of the Chief Information Officers responsible for 
the respective portfolios.  
 
Attachment 2 includes a detailed breakdown of individual project spend by portfolio compared to 
the budgeted spend for each of those projects. 
 
II. 
Program Categories/Spending Rationales 
 
National Grid has re-organized the US Information Technology organization into six areas:

IT capital investment is tracked based on these area designations. Descriptions of each portfolio 
category/spending rationale are provided below. 
 
Group Functions  
Group Functions executes National Grid’s digital roadmaps, leveraging technology and 
reimagining processes in support of Finance, Enterprise Business Services, Human Resources, 
Legal, and Safety Health & Environmental, continuing to upgrade SOX related systems, and 
retiring outdated systems. 
 
United States Electric 
Provides IT Support to our US Electric Distribution and Transmission businesses.  Modernizing 
our key legacy operational systems while building capabilities that will enable the energy transition 
and transformation to a Distribution System Operator (DSO).   Through digital delivery, the 
Electric CIO organization provides greater efficiency and data driven insights into our workforce 
operations that provide:  
 More automated and reliable grid controls systems  
 Capital programs and projects that support the proliferation of Distributed Energy 
Resources (DERs)  
 A growing market of prosumer electric customers 
 
United States Gas 
Provides IT Support to our US Gas Distribution and Transmission businesses by developing digital 
products based on the foundation of gas business enablement that deliver continuous improvement 
of our asset lifecycle management capabilities through:   
 Risk-based asset investment planning  
 Performance-based maintenance  
 AI-based work optimization  
 Mobile field products 
 
Customer 
Provides IT Support to our US Customer business, delivering best-in-class digital products that 
increase engagement and reduce costs to serve by:  
 Modernizing our legacy “back-end” IT estate to support more digital products  
 Liberating data and creating an abstracted and real-time customer data platform to assist 
with achieving energy efficiency targets

Digital Platforms and Infrastructure Technology (DPIT) (Formerly Infrastructure and Operations) 
Supports our internal IT Architecture covering Cloud and Hosting, Critical Network Infrastructure, 
Networks, End User Experience and Operations.  DPIT is focused on reducing National Grid’s 
technical debt through cost effective, modernized IT infrastructure, enabling cloud capabilities that 
meet our risk profile.   The organization enables a connected, seamless enterprise that is flexible, 
secure, reliable and scalable while maintaining acceptable levels of technical debt and risk. 
 
Security 
The Security function protects our people, premises, and digital systems with the objective of 
maintaining trust in National Grid services, focusing on: 
• 
Reduction in likelihood and impact of security incidents 
• 
Compliance with relevant laws, standards and regulations (e.g., NERC, PCI DSS, 
GDPR, NIS-R) 
• 
Improved user experience and standard of security practices across National Grid 
 
The Security function aims to reduce the likelihood and impact of physical and cyber security 
incidents affecting National Grid. It does this by championing security best practices, technology, 
and promoting a security-awareness culture.  
 
Other Category 
 
For accounting purposes there is an additional category listed in Attachment 2 to this report.   The 
“Other” category has 3 elements;  
• 
The “IT4IT” sub-category is essentially a funding bucket for NPV-positive projects 
to enable efficiency savings in our IT-run the business operations.   
• 
The “Other” sub-category is the allocation of operating expense overheads such as 
Enterprise Architecture and Solution Delivery charges to a centralized account.   
The capital charges for this overhead are made directly to individual projects.    
• 
Finally, “Burdens” are the net removal of operating expense burdens to ensure our 
reporting agrees to our Corporate Controllable Cost reporting.   Operating expense 
burdens are consolidated and reported separately under non-controllable costs in 
our corporate reporting packs.

2. Portfolio Sections – The remainder of Attachment 1 includes six sections, one for each 
of the portfolios: Group Functions; US Gas; US Electric; Customer; DPIT; and 
Security.   Each portfolio consists of 3 pages: 
a. The first page provides a narrative financial and business overview.   The three 
charts on the first page show: (1) operating expenses; (2) capital expenses; and, 
(3) total expenses. Each chart shows FY22 actuals by period versus budget, with 
trend lines showing prior year expenditure and run rate.   This page also shows 
the full year Q4 actual total expenditure compared to the Q4 budget. 
b. The second page of the portfolio sections has one chart on the top left of the 
page. This chart compares full fiscal year actual expenditure versus annual 
budget, by program.  A priority investments list for the portfolio and their status 
appears at the top right hand of the page.  Blue means complete, green means 
on track, amber means some risk, and red means focused intervention required. 
On the bottom half of this page is a chart showing actual spend for FY22 
compared to budget, prior year and run rate for the portfolio.   Each bar is color-
coded to give an overview of the comparative spend per program. 
c. The third page of each portfolio section provides a status update on the various 
projects that are active, complete, and in the pipeline, as well as the 
methodology by which we are delivering the projects.  There is also a key 
challenges section and the escalation point for that challenge. 
 
Attachment 1 is based on National Grid’s monthly Strategic Portfolio Reviews (SPR) 
and reporting cadence to senior management of each portfolio, and ultimately to the IT 
leadership team.  Security and DPIT do not currently participate in the SPR reviews 
but provide their respective senior management with monthly updates.

(1) Total actual spend compared to budget and variance.   
(2) A variance reason for all capital investments which are outside the 10% 
tolerance to budget. 
  
C. Attachment 3

(1) The list of closure papers written and approved in FY22 
(2) Total costs incurred in the closure papers 
(3) Explanation of the benefits derived from the closure papers 
(4) Summary of important/relevant lessons learned 
 
In total, 105 projects were closed during FY22 with a total cost of $259.693 million.

National Grid 
Executive Summary – US IT
Financial Summary
US IT faced significant headwinds this year that caused delays across our investment plans. Staffing shortages, SME availability, supply chain issues, and divesture
challenges all impacted progress.
We were able to offset underspend in portfolios by pulling in out year investments and accelerating work where appropriate and
advantageous. Notwithstanding the challenges, significant progress has been made with reducing technical debt (23.9%) and delivering capabilities to benefit both our
internal and external customers. Key achievements were delivering the Unified Web Portal in Downstate New York, Future Now (data driven investment planning tool),
Vegetation Management Optimization and Transmission Outage for our Electric Business.
We continue to invest heavily in cyber security to mitigate threats to our assets.
Many of the challenges the business faced this year 
impacted the wider economy.
Capacity and Resources
1. Availability of IT and business resources to support
delivery
2. Recruiting and retaining high quality permanent
resources is proving challenging
3. Significant change across the organization
4. Covid related issues with third-party contractor
resource pools (earlier in year)
Supply Chain Issues 
Commercial and Contracting Challenges, Supply Chain 
issues and chip shortages
Divestures 
Portfolios have been impacted with separation leading 
to potential delays and stoppage of work to ensure 
oversight of investments for the benefit of our remaining 
customers.

Executive Summary - Group Functions
Financial Summary
Budget ($M)
69.2
Totex
We executed our FY22 portfolio plan to meet budget expectations and delivering 97% of Capex to Budget. Key delivered capabilities include: (1) Blackline - delivering labor efficiencies 
through automation, communications, and enhanced accuracy and accountability; (2) FERC Forms - federal mandate upgrading form submission system resulting in automated 
regulatory filings and improved business information processing; (3) HR Service Pack - deliver needed updates to the SAP application portfolio in order to comply with federal, state, and 
local government requirements ; (4) BW Consolidation - consolidating two separate reporting platforms into one, reducing cost of IT support and hardware; (5) Pension Admin. 
Replacement – delivers reduced administrative costs and provides a better user experience for both plan sponsor and participants; (6) 401(k) Enhancements - merging two 401(k) 
plans into one resulting in participant savings of 30% year over year and adding a Roth 401(k) to the plan, meeting the needs of our multi-generational workforce. 
Summary
•
OPEX variance of $5.8m was the main driver of
the overall variance of $7.5m to TOTEX budget,
due in part to the general industry challenges
experienced across IT that delayed the OPEX
intensive start and closure phases of certain
investments
Significant Project Updates
•
Palantir-mandated walk-in added spend of $2.9m
not previously budgeted
•
SAP landscape added spend of $3.6m spend to
set up SAP project environments
•
MyHub $6.3m and Fieldglass $1.8m underspend
due to business constraints leading spend to shift
from FY22 to FY23
•
Source to Pay Transformation spend
of $3M shifted from FY22 to FY23 due to contract
license negotiations with SAP
•
GridStack infrastructure investment progressed
through SGA and sanctioning to deliver in Q4 of
FY22 with additional $10.2m spend
•
Cloud Migration required additional $2.0m for

Totex
The November release of Gas Business Enablement (GBE) successfully added 1,200+ users of Long Island to the GBE solution and work has switched to the MA and NYC (May 2022) Release:  
Detailed planning is underway for post-Nov against May scenarios optimizing data and training management. 
The US Gas business delivered: (1) NRG GIS replacement - convert and move data from an unstable GIS platform to an enterprise strategic format and stable platform that helps the business 
with less outages and business continuity plans; (2) Interfaced MyHub To Onboard LMS OQ External Site - built an employee information interface between SAP/MyHub and Gas Operational 
Qualifications (OQ) certification provider (ITS) to eliminate errors due to manual processing and reduce fines and re-work performed by field technicians; (3) Primavera Upgrade/Stabilization -
provides a significant expansion in functionality for complex capital gas and electric project planning, scheduling, and forecasting activities, including risk management and new web-enabled / 
mobile capabilities that will help better decision making for complex capital projects risks, costs and forecast accuracy; (4) PIF replacement - platform upgrade that reduces security risk and 
complexity for maintenance and support; (5) Minimum Viable Product release for LNG Asset & Work management - implemented asset and work management framework to track and 
proactively maintain assets of LNG plants throughout their lifecyle on an enterprise platform.
The general industry challenges impacted the Gas portfolio 
but we were able to manage delays by substitutions and 
pulling work forward.   
•
Stabilization of Critical Gas Legacy Applications - $1.6m
incremental spend to address the security risks and
platform stability of enterprise platforms (Salesforce,
Maximo and MuleSoft) that would reduce the numbers of
P1/P2 incidents and reallocation of resources from support
to other priorities.  However, much of the planned work has
been delayed until FY23 ($6.6m).
•
Continuous improvement for Gas applications $3m -
Schedule and resourcing enhancement work for Gas
Business.
•
Pathfinder for Leak Survey which only impacts the MA
jurisdiction $7m. The effort was to replace the Palm pilot
standalone application with existing integration to access
database.
•
Summons for Corrective Actions and LNG IT for OT
support were postponed to FY23 due to resource
challenges and technical issues $3.4m.
•
Gas I&R, Meter Ops, and field device replacement was
moved to FY23 due to late schedule of laptops from the
supplier $2.5m.
•
Capital Delivery - Safety and Risk Artificial Intelligence in
the Field – Proof of concept was run by the business before
a decision to proceed was made $1m.

13
National Grid 
Executive Summary – US Electric
Financial Summary
In FY22, Electric IT Focused On –
1) Reducing operational risk by upgrading / replacing end of life systems, e.g., Energy Accounting System Migration to Wholesale Settlement application, US Control-Transmission
Outage Application (iTOA) application upgrade, MV90 (in-flight – application captures Electric Meter Read for Commercial/ Industrial/Wholesale Customers which supports 40% of
Electric Revenue), and Field Collection System Upgrade (in-flight)
2) Re-imagining ways of working for Field Employees, providing them with new Business Capabilities to help drive operational efficiencies through the releases of new and
transformational Digital products: 
• Vegetation Management Optimization (VMO): Minimum viable product (MVP) was launched on Nov 15th, providing capabilities to leverage and drive a reduction in contractor costs by optimizing our
cycle prune and hazard tree removal plans. This product drove $2.04M in Type 1 Contractor Savings in FY22 and is expected to drive $4.47M in FY23.
•
OnMyWay: Enables electric field crews to self-assign short cycle jobs while in the field. Through the end of the year, Field Workers were self-assigning work at an average of 74% for all short cycle
jobs, with some barns reporting 99-100% self-assignment. These self-assignments are done based on experience or guidance from supervisors, which enables our field force to be more
efficient. Through the end of our FY, the team/product achieved $3.2M in actual benefits since initiation.
•
FutureNow:  Launched MVP on February 14th, providing the business with a more accurate, data driven, TOTEX planning tool. Through its simulation and optimization capabilities, this tool will enable
the business to significantly reduce the costs of future Distribution and Transmission workplan; FY23 benefits are expected to be $10M CAPEX and $1.5M OPEX.
*Forecast updated subsequent to input into financial systems

National Grid 
Executive Summary – Customer
Financial Summary
Budget ($M)
51.5
Actual ($M)
52.0
Totex
Customer is making significant strides in digital enablement and improving the customer experience. Two advancements of note in Q4 include a major AMI milestone and 
increased adoption of our Business Customer on the My Business Account platform. The AMI team successfully connected live meters to AMI applications in lab and 
generating bills. Momentum continues in Q1 as end-to-end testing progresses well.  My Business Account adoption reached 20.05% by the end of FY22 - this provides our 
business customers the ability to pay and manage multiple accounts, provides them insights into their energy use, and allows them to better manage their solar credits.
The Customer portfolio utilized the full budget for 
the year with a small variance to target.
The largest variance is in the Unified Web Portal 
(UWP – our new transaction web portal) project. 
After the UWP launch in November to NYC Gas 
Customers, we have had stability issues due to 
multiple root causes including bad data; missing or 
incorrect user profiles; software errors; and poorly 
tuned servers. From a customer perspective, this 
would have resulted in poor transaction response 
times, or even, in very rare occasions, transaction 
time-outs. The additional resources required to 
stabilize the experience is the primary driver of 
additional costs. The UWP project will continue to 
run over budget into Q1 FY23 for launch readiness.. 
In Q4 we decided to delay the re-start of the new 
Smart Target tool in order to focus on higher priority 
efforts.  That is the primary driver of the Q3 forecast 
miss.  We intend to re-start Smart Target in the 
second half of FY23.

National Grid 
Executive Summary – Security
Financial Summary
Budget ($M)
36.4
Actual ($M)
34.0
Totex
Security has prioritized delivery of key risk reducing Security Capabilities into Operational Technology environments, while sustaining capabilities established in the 
Enterprise and Critical National Infrastructure environments with consideration of the changing threat landscape. The US Operational Technology Engineering Team has 
on-boarded the necessary resources to establish Security Point of Presence at identified Operational Sites. The Identity and Access Management Program is set to close 
in the first quarter of the upcoming fiscal year.
Security Portfolio 
Security experienced similar challenges to the 
rest of the industry in terms of supply chain and 
resourcing issues.   
The threats to our networks are constantly 
evolving and require monitoring to ensure 
threats are mitigated.  As a result, funds were 
reprioritized across the portfolio to relieve these 
pressures.
This has led to acceleration of the Identity and 
Access Management Program, and the 
prioritization of reducing risk at Operational 
Technology sites.
Total spend was in line with the budget 
allocation across the cyber investments. 
Physical security was underspent by $2m due 
to break/fix actuals being less than original 
estimates.

Category
Type of Variance
Explanation
Project Delivery ‐ Scope change
Scope changes  
 Spend impacted by both reduced or increased scope
Project Delivery ‐ Initial scope delivered
Imprecise Estimates 
 Cost and Quantity of resources were incorrectly assessed when creating the budget. (eg. 
Price Increases)
Project Delivery ‐ Initial scope delivered
Complexity 
 Unforeseen challenges in delivering the solution drove costs up.   No change in scope but 
amount of work to deliver increased or potentially decreased
Project Delivery ‐ Initial scope delivered
Efficiencies 
 More cost effective implementation options ‐ Found a better way to deliver the solution 
which reduced costs
Strategic Direction
Funding Bucket 
 Source of undefined funding where funds will be moved to other projects
Strategic Direction
Funding Change
Move $ to or from another project 
Annual Accounting
Accounting
Over or under accruals which reverse at year end leaving a balance on the INVP
Annual Accounting
Timing
Project slipped and intended scope was not delivered this fiscal year

Other

$1,668,000 What went well - The MS Teams project was launched as COVID-19 Emergency project to increase IT capability 
for staff to work from home. The tight timeframe for delivery required a deviation from the normal protocols for 
project delivery. The necessary measures were given the full support of management and the project teams 
adapted admiralty to the challenges ahead. This resulted in MS Teams being enabled for circa 25,000 users 
within 6 weeks.
What went well - The urgency to deliver a swift solution meant that the usual Governance and Service Transition 
approach would not naturally fit to the aggressive implementation timeline. 
Governance and Service Transition continue to show process flexibility to accommodate urgent project delivery. 
It's noted that the Governance and Service Transition processes have recently been adapted to accommodate 
the new Agile Delivery approach in I&O. 
What didn't go so well - Native MS Teams does allow end users to create their own Teams however this solution 
did not fulfill security requirements. The operational model approach, i.e. raise a service now ticket had a 
Service Level Agreement of 5 days to create a Team. This wasn't acceptable to management. During the project 
an interim solution was implemented with a request form in SharePoint and a dedicated member of the Project 
Team who created Teams. The turnaround time for this process was 1-4 hours which set an expectation for the 
end user community. 
Recommendation - Earlier review of the solutions being sought and thorough impact analysis against the risk 
that the desired solution may be delayed. 
Revisit alternative solutions, previously discounted to see if they can be adapted to meet the need in a shorter 
timeframe.
 NaƟonal Grid is a global organizaƟon that builds teams that deliver business goals.  There is no expectaƟon that 
those teams are co-located and team members are frequently based in different offices or even different 
regions.
A greater choice of tools will improve the opportunities for teams to select the right tools for their needs and 
allow them to become productive in a shorter space of time.

changes for billing in the Customer Services System (CSS) accordingly.

$705,000 The scope of the discovery phase of the project was set without full consideration for the future use of the

Ensure adequate time is allowed in the startup phase to develop the project delivery approach and to reach

Improved governance in pipeline planning and reporting.
The approach to sanction a group of similar projects into a program results in complex management of program 
finances and sanctions. This is especially true if the projects are of differing durations and global. Re-sanction at 
program level is often required only for one of the projects in the program, resulting in frequent sanction steps. 
Either progress sanction at the project level or allow wider flexibility for program sanctions to cover longer time 
periods & stages and be governed by PMB or Product Owner.
 NaƟonal Grid uƟlizes mulƟple instances of SharePoint (2007, 2010, 2013) leading to inconsistencies in control, 
support and site storage. To lower IT operational spend and ensure only systems within support are used, 
National Grid has consolidated the numerous SharePoint instances into SharePoint Online.

The Network Security Infrastructure Program was initiated for a series of projects intended to refresh the 
network infrastructure and provide new capabilities to improve network performance, mobility and user 
experience.
To ensure that the services continued to be secure, reliable and efficient it was important that services were 
maintained within support and new capabilities were added as technology advanced.  In addition, the changing 
threat landscape and expanding use of cloud based services required a change from premise based security 
appliances towards more agile cloud and virtual security platforms.  The program prioritized work and delivered 
the most critical first, considering current and future needs of the business.
The purpose of this program paper was initially to request funds for the following initiatives listed under the 
Program INVP 5522 - Network Security Infrastructure Program:
5522A: Verizon – End User Virtual Private Network (VPN) Replacement
5522C: Verizon – Verizon Strategic Internet Gateway (vSTIG) Device Refresh
5522D: Verizon – Verizon - Tufin Upgrade
5522F: Verizon – vSTIG re-architecture - New Core Firewall
The only project completed under this program was: INVP 5522A: Verizon - End User Virtual Private Network 
(VPN) Replacement
The remaining projects were de-scoped and defunded from this program: 
5522C - vSTIG refresh was completed under a separate initiative in FY21, INVP 6037 for the upgrade and 
hardware refresh is part of FY22 Network initiative sanction
5522D - not addressed under any other initiatives
5522F - this work was to be owned by the IT Security Group

Gas Control Center Simulator F&A
$0
$253,082
$253,082  IdenƟfy scope and validate if other NG IT teams are needed for the project to ensure no cost variance in the end 
of the project.
RFP timelines depend on the vendor engagement, hence get commitment for vendors on timely responses and 
include risk margin to accommodate and delays to stay on top of schedule slips.   
 This is a Feasibility & Analysis study. The purpose of this phase of the project was to select a SCADA Gas Control 
Simulator software vendor that can provide software to allow extensive "almost on-the-job training" for Gas 
Control operators, without adversely impacting the gas distribution and transmission network.
The idea is that Gas Controllers in the Control Center will be able to simulate various situations that occur on the 
production SCADA system and train in a disconnected environment to handle such situations, without actually 
causing any harm, if something were to not go as planned.

$307,614 After considerable analysis, the CWQ project team determined that is was impossible to upgrade the planned 
components without upgrading the entire application.  Consequently, we obtained approval from the CWQ 
business sponsor (Caroline Hon) to repurpose CWQ’s QA Environment as a DR Fail-over site, and conclude the 
CWQ project by handing off to Production Support the DR Fail-over Runbook and configuration definition.  
Therefore, the knowledge transfer session with the Production Support team was completed on 22 Feb 2021.  
During this session,  details of the DR Fail-over Runbook and Hardware / Software Configuration Matrix were 
delivered, thereby illustrating that assets were delivered through the suite of DR Fail-over documentation 
provided to Production Support Team.  
The original focus of the CWQ project was to upgrade the Citrix servers (or replace Citrix with an alternate 
application virtualization technology), thereby stabilizing the application and improving its performance.  
Following considerable evaluation / research, the CWQ team reached the conclusion that It is not possible to 
upgrade the planned components without upgrading the entire application. Since many of the application’s 
components are no longer offered by their vendor, this would require customization of a replacement 
component.  
Upgrading any of these legacy components would result in the need to upgrade not just the entire CWQ 
application, but all MQ instances within interfacing applications.  This is well beyond the original scope 
anticipated for this project.
Consequently, we have discussed this project conclusion alternative with the CWQ business sponsor, and she 
agreed with repurposing of CWQ’s QA Environment as DR Fail-over site and concluding the CWQ project.  By 
taking this minimum cost alternative, availability of the Production environment will be elevated considerably in 
the event of a major outage.    Acknowledging that the CWQ application must continue to function in Production 
until its replacement by GBE MAXIMO initiative (18 – 24 months).

3. Improvement - Governance: The Cognitive Contract Management (CCM) project was bundled with PowerPlan 
Lease and sanctioned together as a single Investment. The projects ran on 2 very different timelines and it often 
became difficult to manage CCM individually. PowerPlan Lease had higher visibility and CCM issues/risks were 
often less of a priority.   A complex project like CCM should  be sanctioned and managed as its own project to 
ensure it receives the appropriate focus that is required.
4. Improvement - Technical Delivery: IT security review of the application occurred too late in the process.

architecture prior to the start of implementation. At the time Security requested additional requirements, the 
project timeline was impacted. Early and ongoing conversations regarding technical security / non-functional 
requirements is needed to reach a common understanding of these types of requirements to proactively 
mitigate risk and delays.

home related to the COVID-19 pandemic. The testing team on this project was required to focus all of its time 
on ensuring a success virtual year end close.

5570
Electric Field Crew iPad Time Entry 
and Basic Capability -NE
$942,000
$0
$942,000 1. Project team learned how to successfully re-design the training effort to deliver remotely rather than in-
person due to Covid restrictions.
2. The remote training method provided the benefit of flexibility for Operations, removing one or two field 
personnel rather than a classroom full, thus lessening the impact of the training. It also was flexible in that last 
minute changes could be made with individuals either reporting out sick or needed on an emergency job.
3. Since the remote training was conducted one on one, it was tailored to the individual, creating a better overall 
experience.
4. With remote training, the philosophy was changed to offer training slots for an entire region rather than one 
physical facility, increasing the efficiency in which the training could be completed. 
5. We learned that the team had to set some days aside for building and distributing of the iPads since the 
remote trainings were consuming the entire day rather than just the mornings as in the past classroom setting.
This project drove the replacement of a manual paper process for the capture and entry of field crew time 
leading to increased accuracy, reduce delays and improve efficiencies for field crew time capture. A  suite of 
tools was introduced which  allowed the field to remotely access the latest standards and operating manuals 
reducing the need to print paper and carry paper copies in the trucks. Crews have remote access to Maps, 
facility records and safety information improving improved awareness and safety in
the field
 
Direct cost savings (Annual):
 - Cost savings will be from paper reduction in MA and RI 
 - Indirect financial benefits:
 - Safety – reduces injury and risk to employees and customers
 - Technology platform – basis for future digital initiatives
 - Improved data quality – reduce time entry data errors

6097
Cloud Video Interoperability
$1,171,000
$1,000
$1,172,000 Cloud Video Interop (CVI) was implemented on circa 170 devices globally. Given the impact comprehensive 
testing would have on time, resource effort and cost it was decided to conduct a full test over a weekend across 
a selected number of video conference rooms (15 in total) and all other rooms were tested against a minimum 
viable product set of test cases.
 - Consider a similar approach for future work where there is a requirement for repetitive testing.
 
COVID site access restrictions and geographical distances between sites required the support of team members 
outside of the Project Team. The Project Team were thankful for support from the US Exec Support Teams who 
were often on site or closer to site and were not subject to the tighter site access restrictions implemented due 
to COVID.
 - When faced with on site testing at a variety of locations consider the option of utilizing local resource.
 
The CVI extended feature One Button to Join (OBTJ) was not included in the original project scope.
 - Consider the benefits of including the complete service in the original scope versus the option of delivering the 
MVP solution and then retrofitting additional features.
 - Enabled Video Conference Devices to facilitate Microsoft Teams meetings 
 - Reduced the number of WebEx licenses required to facilitate meetings using video conference devices

5523G
Downstate NY PBX Replacement 
Upgrade
$381,000
$80,000
$461,000  1. The AS-IS documentaƟon needs to be maintained by NaƟonal Grid and not by third-party vendors. There was 
no documentation for the control room phones within National Grid. It is recommended that new 
documentation should have all published listed for each control room.
2. Existing control rooms with Cisco phones must be treated like new control rooms which led to performing 
development and full user acceptance testing at locations.
3. Resiliency plans for control rooms using a call from home can have issues if jabber fails and the cell phone 
takes too long to ring in some areas. The recommended action is; for smaller control rooms we should 
implement Normal Call Flow and emergency call flow, Emergency Call Flow rings all jabber phones, desk phones, 
and cell phones immediately, and larger control rooms may need to incorporate cell phones into a normal call 
flow.
The key business benefits are to have:
 - The new voice recording system will comply with Section 215 of the Federal Power Act (FPA), which requires 
control room calls to be retained for three years.
 - The legacy voice recording system is at a critical risk of unrecoverable failure. The system is no longer vendor-
supported and has had failures that have resulted in the loss of recording capability.
 - The recording system is on Windows 2000 operating system, which is no longer vendor supported.
 - Modern, supported, and reliable telephony infrastructure to record incoming and outgoing calls into Gas 
Dispatch.
 - Ease of the Maintenance.
 - The ability to playback recorded calls reliably as and when needed, in order to meet business, regulatory, and 
audit needs.
 - A better Quality Control process to streamline how we receive calls, retrieve information, and communicate 
that information to internal and external customers.
 - Enhanced end-user experience.
 - This project is aligned to the strategies of National Grid.

Information Technology Capital Investment Report for  
Quarter Ended June 30, 2022 
 
 
I. 
Introduction 
 
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submit this Information Technology (“IT”) Capital Investment Quarterly Report 
(“IT Quarterly Report”) for the first quarter of fiscal year 2023 (“FY23”).1  Pursuant to the Public 
Service Commission’s (“Commission”) January 20, 2022 Order in Cases 20-E-0380 and 20-G-
0381, and August 12, 2021 Order in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-0310, the Company is to provide 
quarterly variance reports to Department of Public Service Staff (“Staff”) regarding IT capital 
projects and investments.2  The IT Quarterly Report provides an explanation of the Company’s 
overall IT investment plan approach; descriptions of program investment categories; and a 
comparison of budgeted to actual spending. 
 
IT capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s operating 
companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. (“Service 
Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara Mohawk, 
KEDNY and KEDLI, in the form of Service Company rent expense once the investments are in-
service.  The Service Company rent expense includes a return on the capital investment (net of 
deferred taxes) plus booked depreciation expense. 
 
Through Q1 FY23, National Grid spent $59.3 million compared to a year-to-date Service 
Company budget of $65.0 million, representing a $5.7 million underspend.  Attachment 1 includes 
detail on budgets and actual spending for each of the portfolios and commentary regarding 
performance which has been presented to each of the Chief Information Officers responsible for 
the respective portfolios.  
 
Attachment 2 includes a detailed breakdown of individual project spend by portfolio compared to 
the budgeted spend for each of those investments. 
 
II. 
Program Categories/Spending Rationales 
 
National Grid has re-organized the US Information Technology organization into six areas:

IT capital investment is tracked based on these area designations. Descriptions of each portfolio 
category/spending rationale are provided below. 
 
Group Functions  
Group Functions executes National Grid’s digital roadmaps, leveraging technology and 
reimagining processes in support of Finance, Enterprise Business Services, Human Resources, 
Legal, and Safety Health & Environmental, continuing to upgrade SOX related systems, and 
retiring outdated systems. 
 
United States Electric 
Provides IT Support to our US Electric Distribution and Transmission businesses.  Modernizing 
our key legacy operational systems while building capabilities that will enable the energy transition 
and transformation to a Distribution System Operator (DSO).   Through digital delivery, the 
Electric CIO organization provides greater efficiency and data driven insights into our workforce 
operations that provide:  
 More automated and reliable grid controls systems  
 Capital programs and projects that support the proliferation of Distributed Energy 
Resources (DERs)  
 A growing market of prosumer electric customers 
 
United States Gas 
Provides IT Support to our US Gas Distribution and Transmission businesses by developing digital 
products based on the foundation of gas business enablement that deliver continuous improvement 
of our asset lifecycle management capabilities through:   
 Risk-based asset investment planning  
 Performance-based maintenance  
 AI-based work optimization  
 Mobile field products 
 
Customer 
Provides IT Support to our US Customer business, delivering best-in-class digital products that 
increase engagement and reduce costs to serve by:  
 Modernizing our legacy “back-end” IT estate to support more digital products  
 Liberating data and creating an abstracted and real-time customer data platform to assist 
with achieving energy efficiency targets

Digital Platforms and Infrastructure Technology (DPIT) (Formerly Infrastructure and Operations) 
Supports our internal IT Architecture covering Cloud and Hosting, Critical Network Infrastructure, 
Networks, End User Experience and Operations.  DPIT is focused on reducing National Grid’s 
technical debt through cost effective, modernized IT infrastructure, enabling cloud capabilities that 
meet our risk profile.   The organization enables a connected, seamless enterprise that is flexible, 
secure, reliable and scalable while maintaining acceptable levels of technical debt and risk. 
 
Security 
The Security function protects our people, premises, and digital systems with the objective of 
maintaining trust in National Grid services, focusing on: 
• 
Reduction in likelihood and impact of security incidents 
• 
Compliance with relevant laws, standards and regulations (e.g., NERC, PCI DSS, 
GDPR, NIS-R) 
• 
Improved user experience and standard of security practices across National Grid 
 
The Security function aims to reduce the likelihood and impact of physical and cyber security 
incidents affecting National Grid. It does this by championing security best practices, technology, 
and promoting a security-awareness culture.  
 
Other Category 
 
For accounting purposes there is an additional category listed in Attachment 2 to this report.   The 
“Other” category has 3 elements: 
• 
The “IT4IT” sub-category acts as a funding bucket for NPV-positive projects to 
enable efficiency savings in our IT-run business operations.   
• 
The “Other” sub-category is the allocation of operating expense overheads such as 
Enterprise Architecture and Solution Delivery charges to a centralized account.   
The capital charges for this overhead are made directly to individual projects.    
• 
Finally, “Burdens” are the net removal of operating expense burdens to ensure our 
reporting agrees with our Corporate Controllable Cost reporting.   Operating 
expense burdens are consolidated and reported separately under non-controllable 
costs in our corporate reporting packs.

• SBP22 efforts are wrapping up and have been a

challenges and global supply chain issues (i.e.

being managed and do not require escalation at this
time. All Core Products that were expected to be
delivered in FY23 remain on track to do so.
• Q1 Total spend was $5.7M less than Budget; $2.7m
was in digital products with the remainder across the
portfolio largely due to mobilization efforts and
ramping up of resources.
• FY23 Forecast is currently running ~$1.1m under
target with the potential for these funds to be used
for other products and Business needs (i.e.
CNI/EMS Enhancements, Computapole F&A, etc.)
