Portfolio Commentary
• All Q1 budgeted efforts have active delivery teams 
with no lag in delivery at the start of the year. 
• Q1 spend exceeded budget due primarily to 
Unified Wed Portal digital re-architecture and 
optimization.  The current forecast for the year is 
to overspend by $6m, however there is upward 
pressure to spend $10M more than budget to 
deliver UWP 2.0 and IVR Re-platform.  We are 
reviewing opportunities to re-allocate funding 
within the US IT portfolio to cover this demand. 
• In Q1 we had continuous delivery on products to 
improve customer experience, improve efficiency 
and meet regulatory mandates.  Of note were 
eight updates to the IVR call flow to improve 
service through that channel and saving 
$200k/month with higher containment, significant 
enhancements on recurring pay and notifications 
for our C&I customers in the My Business Account 
product and automating the EAP billing 
functionality for the KEDLI rate case.  
• Looking ahead, we have had major releases in Q2 
to-date including extending the Unified Web Portal 
to the final territories, LI and UNY, AMI MVP 
delivered with 5 live meters producing bills, 
significant improvements to the stability of core 
systems with the FCP upgrade and completed 
remediation to ensure PCI compliance.

• All Product portfolios 100% sanctioned and inflight,
mostly on-track to Outcomes and Key Results and
financial forecast
• Data Center Transformation (DCT) is current exception
– chip shortage, global supply chain issues, and

Release Train
• Operations: Unified Technology Operations Centre
(UTOC) will be a single operations center providing
overwatch of Enterprise, CNI and Operational
technology to maximize security and health of National
Grid assets.
• Minimum Viable Product (MVP) on track; 80%
complete staffing for MVP; Construction delay due to
Safety and HASP paperwork being completed by our
construction vendor.
• Financials lagging slightly behind forecast in Q1 but this
will be recovered in Q2/3,
• Primary drivers are Digital Workplace Services
(DWS) hardware and DCT Mainframe.

Information Technology Capital Investment Report for  
Quarter Ended September 30, 2022 
 
 
I. 
Introduction 
 
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submit this Information Technology (“IT”) Capital Investment Quarterly Report 
(“IT Quarterly Report”) for the second quarter (Q2) of fiscal year 2023 (“FY23”).1  Pursuant to 
the Public Service Commission’s (“Commission”) January 20, 2022 Order in Cases 20-E-0380 
and 20-G-0381, and August 12, 2021 Order in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-0310, the Company is 
to provide quarterly variance reports to Department of Public Service Staff (“Staff”) regarding IT 
capital projects and investments.2  The IT Quarterly Report provides an explanation of the 
Company’s overall IT investment plan approach, descriptions of program investment categories, 
and a comparison of budgeted to actual spending. 
 
IT capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s operating 
companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. (“Service 
Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara Mohawk, 
KEDNY, and KEDLI, in the form of Service Company rent expense once the investments are in-
service.  The Service Company rent expense includes a return on the capital investment (net of 
deferred taxes) plus booked depreciation expense. 
 
Through Q2 FY23, National Grid spent $144.9 million compared to a year-to-date Service 
Company budget of $146.9 million, representing a $1.9 million underspend.  Attachment 1 
includes detail on budgets and actual spending for each of the portfolios and commentary regarding 
performance which has been presented to each of the Chief Information Officers responsible for 
the respective portfolios.  
 
Attachment 2 includes a detailed breakdown of individual project spend by portfolio compared to 
the budgeted spend for each of those investments. 
 
II. 
Program Categories/Spending Rationales 
 
National Grid has organized the US Information Technology organization into six areas:

IT capital investment is tracked based on these area designations. Descriptions of each portfolio 
category/spending rationale are provided below. 
 
Group Functions  
Group Functions executes National Grid’s digital roadmaps, leveraging technology and 
reimagining processes in support of Finance, Enterprise Business Services, Human Resources, 
Legal, and Safety Health & Environmental, continuing to upgrade SOX related systems, and 
retiring outdated systems. 
 
United States Electric 
Provides IT Support to our US Electric Distribution and Transmission businesses.  Modernizing 
our key legacy operational systems while building capabilities that will enable the energy transition 
and transformation to a Distribution System Operator (DSO).   Through digital delivery, the 
Electric CIO organization provides greater efficiency and data driven insights into our workforce 
operations that provide:  
 More automated and reliable grid controls systems  
 Capital programs and projects that support the proliferation of Distributed Energy 
Resources (DERs)  
 A growing market of prosumer electric customers 
 
United States Gas 
Provides IT Support to our US Gas Distribution and Transmission businesses by developing digital 
products based on the foundation of gas business enablement that deliver continuous improvement 
of our asset lifecycle management capabilities through:   
 Risk-based asset investment planning  
 Performance-based maintenance  
 AI-based work optimization  
 Mobile field products 
 
Customer 
Provides IT Support to our US Customer business, delivering best-in-class digital products that 
increase engagement and reduce costs to serve by:  
 Modernizing our legacy “back-end” IT estate to support more digital products  
 Liberating data and creating an abstracted and real-time customer data platform to assist 
with achieving energy efficiency targets  
 
 
 
Exhibit ___ (ITDP-2R)

Digital Platforms and Infrastructure Technology (DPIT) (Formerly Infrastructure and Operations) 
Supports our internal IT Architecture covering Cloud and Hosting, Critical Network Infrastructure, 
Networks, End User Experience and Operations.  DPIT is focused on reducing National Grid’s 
technical debt through cost effective, modernized IT infrastructure, enabling cloud capabilities that 
meet our risk profile.   The organization enables a connected, seamless enterprise that is flexible, 
secure, reliable and scalable while maintaining acceptable levels of technical debt and risk. 
 
Security 
The Security function protects our people, premises, and digital systems with the objective of 
maintaining trust in National Grid services, focusing on: 
• 
Reduction in likelihood and impact of security incidents 
• 
Compliance with relevant laws, standards and regulations (e.g., NERC, PCI DSS, 
GDPR, NIS-R) 
• 
Improved user experience and standard of security practices across National Grid 
 
The Security function aims to reduce the likelihood and impact of physical and cyber security 
incidents affecting National Grid. It does this by championing security best practices, technology, 
and promoting a security-awareness culture.  
 
Other Category 
For accounting purposes, there is an additional category listed in Attachment 2 to this report.   The 
“Other” category has 3 elements: 
• 
The “IT4IT” sub-category acts as a funding bucket for NPV-positive projects to 
enable efficiency savings in our IT-run business operations.   
• 
The “Other” sub-category is the allocation of operating expense overheads such as 
Enterprise Architecture and Solution Delivery charges to a centralized account.   
The capital charges for this overhead are made directly to individual projects.    
• 
Finally, “Burdens” are the net removal of operating expense burdens to ensure our 
reporting agrees with our Corporate Controllable Cost reporting.  Operating 
expense burdens are consolidated and reported separately under non-controllable 
costs in our corporate reporting packs.

and run rate.  Each bar is color-coded to give an overview of the comparative 
spend per portfolio (p. 3).

2. Portfolio Sections – The remainder of Attachment 1 includes six sections, one for each 
of the portfolios: Group Functions; US Gas; US Electric; Customer; DPIT; and 
Security.   Each portfolio consists of 3 pages: 
a. The first page provides a narrative financial and business overview.   The three 
charts on the first page show: (1) operating expenses; (2) capital expenses; and, 
(3) total expenses. Each chart shows FY23 actuals and forecast by period versus 
budget, with trend lines showing prior year expenditure and run rate.   This page 
also shows the full year forecast and year to date total and capital expenditure 
compared to the budget. 
b. The second page of the portfolio sections has two charts on the top left of the 
page: the top chart is actual expenditure versus budget by program year to date.  
The second chart compares full fiscal year forecast versus annual budget by 
program.  There is also a key challenges section and the escalation point for that 
challenge.  On the bottom half of this page is a chart showing actual and 
forecasted spend for FY23 compared to budget, prior year and run rate for the 
portfolio.  Each bar is color-coded to give an overview of the comparative spend 
per program.  
c. The third page of each portfolio section provides a status update on the various 
projects.  A priority investments list for the portfolio and their status appears at 
the top right hand of the page. Blue means complete, green means on track, 
amber means some risk, and red means focused intervention required.  
 
Attachment 1 is based on National Grid’s monthly Strategic Portfolio Reviews (SPR) 
and reporting cadence to senior management of each portfolio, and ultimately to the IT 
leadership team.

5
National Grid 
US Gas
Financial Performance
•
U.S. Gas variance is largely due to the CS&E program, which 
is driving the forecast from the original plan and year to date 
variance to budget, with overruns on vendor labor and 
misalignment on where NG labor costs would fall. Re-
sanction for the program is almost complete and we’re on 
forecast with the revised sanction budget. 
•
The Sanction process has been initiated for Gas Meter 
Management System Deployment and Integration (Tesco), 
FY23 - $3.182M, FY24 - $3.203M.
•
Asset Management for LNG had multiple releases in Q2 that 
enabled integration with PowerPlan for unitization of asset 
data to improve asset tracking. It also provided compliance 
and audit reporting.
•
PI replacement project in second phase; enabled interfaces 
with Primavera. It also enabled Service Now to access 
Primavera Unifier for capital project initiation with open 
authorization enabled.
•
Gas I&R, Meter Operations, and field device replacement 
program replaced 124 aging tough books with Win. 10, 
rugged laptops and mitigated cybersecurity risks. Field teams 
now have personas defined for requesting and using laptops.
•
New Storms Response Management System went live in Q2, 
implementing a new SaaS solution that is more reliable and 
automated, replacing an outdated and unsupported tool. This 
new system will digitize securing, mobilizing crews, and 
provides logistical support during storms and restoration 
events.

9
National Grid 
US Electric
Financial Performance
• Year to date under-spend of $10.4M CAPEX and 
$2.5M OPEX is being driven by supply chain delays, 
resource constraints, and various deliverability 
constraints that are delaying the start to planned 
products. 
•
These delays are impacting the full year forecast and 
will reduce forecast v budget by $10.9M.
• Price Transmission successfully went live on 
October 14th. This enabled NGRID to remove a 
legacy vendor platform (tech debt) and build a Price 
Transmission system.   This system receives hourly 
electricity prices a day ahead from the NYISO, based 
on zone. It then calculates our pricing based on the 
electric prices providing data to our Billing dept. to bill 
customers timely and accurately.
• ADMS: Through Q2, 1,040 of 2,800 (37%) US feeders 
are now ADMS ready, further extending our ability to 
visualize, monitor and simulate the Grid in real time; 
the program is on track to reach 50% FY23 Target.
• UTOC (Unified Technology Operations Center) 
MVP was successfully launched on September 1st at 
the Syracuse Office Complex (SOC). This will help 
improve response times to Network Outages, and 
provide additional data/network monitoring capabilities 
with our Remote Radio Devices (RRD) that support 
connectivity to:
•
Advanced Meter Infrastructure (AMI)
•
Volt/Var Optimization (VVO)
•
Fault Location, Isolation & Service Restoration (FLISR)

Portfolio Commentary
• The Customer portfolio remains on track to meet 
additional demand from the business over the initial 
plan.
•
Demand for services has remained steady from Q1 to Q2; 
reallocation of funding identified to meet demand.
•
Unified Web Portal 2.0 – significant driver of the year to 
date increase over budgeted spend; will provide an 
improved user experience.
•
Zero Based Redesign (ZBR) – Continues to drive high 
value on Interactive Voice Response (IVR) (the other 
significant driver to year to date overspend); delivering 
improved user experience and increased number of self-
service customer resolutions.
•
Clean Energy – Project has kicked off while finalizing 
business funding for NY portion of work. Will increase the 
level of customer engagement and third parties requesting 
clean energy products.
•
Technical Debt – Targeting technical debt remediations 
that support the Customer System and the Customer 
offices.
• Major releases in Q2 included;
•
Extending the Unified Web Portal to the final territories, LI 
and UNY.   
•
Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) Minimum Viable 
Product delivered with 5 live meters producing bills.
•
Significant improvements to the stability of core systems 
with the Foundation for Cooperative Processing (FCP) 
upgrade and completed remediation to ensure Payment 
Card Industry (PCI) compliance.
•
Implemented Community Distributed Generation (CDG) 
Net Metering – eliminates manual billing processes of 
customers participating in CDG billing program.

Portfolio Commentary
Overall Group Functions is tracking to budget both year 
to date and full year forecast.
Key Accomplishments Delivered this Fiscal Year
Join to Leave (J2L) 
transformation through MyHub 2.0
• Delivered manager self-serve for org structure changes 
and hiring initiations for a potential reduction in rework 
activities by 40%  (~350 hrs./mth) for the Business 
Services team.
• Digitizing learning - Supports the broader learning 
transformation enabling global learning support using a 
common platform which improves the user experience, 
the new platform provides more digital content which 
saves~9000 hours in face-to-face training annually. 
Warehouse Investment Recovery- Completed release 1 
which digitized the sale of scrap/obsolete materials from 
our warehouses leading to improved user experience and 
an opportunity for increased revenue generation with new 
efficiencies gained by use of a digital solution.  
HR Support Pack Upgrade delivered in Q2 - These are 
mandatory annual changes requested by Federal and 
State agencies, such as the Internal Revenue 
Service (IRS) and various State Departments of Finance, 
as well as different municipalities. These changes must 
be applied to the SAP core solution in order to properly 
reflect employee wages, employee and Company 
withholdings, legal requirements and to comply with 
Federal and State regulatory reporting.

Key Challenges
Challenge
Escalation Point
• Resource constraints due to competing 
priorities and programs for both IT and 
Business resources
• Working with ADAM partners 
to backfill key roles
• Recruitment ongoing to 
supplement with contractors
• Shortage of skilled/trained resources with 
Agile experience to help with transition to 
agile ways of working
• Upskill key resources in both IT 
and the business
• Recruit and hire to fill open 
requistitions
• Risk – Capex moving to Opex due to new 
Finance policy on SaaS could impact ability 
to deliver financial commitments

25
National Grid 
DPIT
Financial Performance
• Financials: Year to date ~$18M favorable to budget 
driven by budget phasing across the portfolio.  
• The change in full year forecast since Q1 is due to OPEX 
cost shifting out of DPIT to Exceptional Funding.  
Otherwise DPIT is forecasting to spend to budget.
• There will be a higher spend rate in the second half of 
the year driven by Ops Unified Technology Operations 
Centre (UTOC), Digital Workplace Services (HW, 
Atos), DCT (Mainframe SW, testing)
• Product Model enabling $29M incremental FY23 
releases prior to year end: 
• Unified Technology Operations Center (UTOC) 
Minimum Viable Product
• Network upgrades
• Deployment of Windows as a Service updates to >23K 
devices
• C&H improvements: to reduce compute resources 
required for applications, simplify application 
authentication, and ensure security stability
• GridStack delivered centralized documentation, 
reusable code and automated data transformation for 
application development
• Technical Debt: Overall reduced to 19.8% (FY23 goal: 
18%)
• FY24 Investment Planning: Product Managers are 
defining product line epics for FY24 for review in Nov/Dec
• Product objectives will align with Infrastructure and 
Business Unit objectives

Page 1 of 4 
 
 
Information Technology Capital Investment Report for  
Quarter Ended December 31, 2022 
 
 
I. 
Introduction 
 
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submit this Information Technology (“IT”) Capital Investment Quarterly Report 
(“IT Quarterly Report”) for the third quarter (Q3) of fiscal year 2023 (“FY23”).1  Pursuant to the 
Public Service Commission’s (“Commission”) January 20, 2022 Order in Cases 20-E-0380 and 
20-G-0381, and August 12, 2021 Order in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-0310, the Company is to 
provide quarterly variance reports to Department of Public Service Staff (“Staff”) regarding IT 
capital projects and investments.2  The IT Quarterly Report provides an explanation of the 
Company’s overall IT investment plan approach, descriptions of program investment categories, 
and a comparison of budgeted to actual spending. 
 
IT capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s operating 
companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. (“Service 
Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara Mohawk, 
KEDNY, and KEDLI, in the form of Service Company rent expense once the investments are in-
service.  The Service Company rent expense includes a return on the capital investment (net of 
deferred taxes) plus booked depreciation expense. 
 
Through Q3 FY23, National Grid spent $235.1 million compared to a year-to-date Service 
Company budget of $239.6 million, representing a $4.5 million underspend.  Attachment 1 
includes detail on budgets and actual spending for each of the portfolios and commentary regarding 
performance which has been presented to each of the Chief Information Officers responsible for 
the respective portfolios.  
 
Attachment 2 includes a detailed breakdown of individual project spend by portfolio compared to 
the budgeted spend for each of those investments.

Program Categories/Spending Rationales

IT capital investment is tracked based on these area designations. Descriptions of each portfolio 
category/spending rationale are provided below. 
 
Group Functions  
Group Functions executes National Grid’s digital roadmaps, leveraging technology and 
reimagining processes in support of Finance, Enterprise Business Services, Human Resources, 
Legal, and Safety Health & Environmental, continuing to upgrade SOX related systems, and 
retiring outdated systems. 
 
United States Electric 
Provides IT Support to our US Electric Distribution and Transmission businesses.  Modernizing 
our key legacy operational systems while building capabilities that will enable the energy transition 
and transformation to a Distribution System Operator (DSO).   Through digital delivery, the 
Electric CIO organization provides greater efficiency and data driven insights into our workforce 
operations that provide:  
 More automated and reliable grid controls systems  
 Capital programs and projects that support the proliferation of Distributed Energy 
Resources (DERs)  
 A growing market of prosumer electric customers 
 
United States Gas 
Provides IT Support to our US Gas Distribution and Transmission businesses by developing digital 
products based on the foundation of gas business enablement that deliver continuous improvement 
of our asset lifecycle management capabilities through:   
 Risk-based asset investment planning  
 Performance-based maintenance  
 AI-based work optimization  
 Mobile field products 
 
Customer 
Provides IT Support to our US Customer business, delivering best-in-class digital products that 
increase engagement and reduce costs to serve by:  
 Modernizing our legacy “back-end” IT estate to support more digital products  
 Liberating data and creating an abstracted and real-time customer data platform to assist 
with achieving energy efficiency targets

Digital Platforms and Infrastructure Technology (DPIT) (Formerly Infrastructure and Operations) 
Supports our internal IT Architecture covering Cloud and Hosting, Critical Network Infrastructure, 
Networks, End User Experience and Operations.  DPIT is focused on reducing National Grid’s 
technical debt through cost effective, modernized IT infrastructure, enabling cloud capabilities that 
meet our risk profile.   The organization enables a connected, seamless enterprise that is flexible, 
secure, reliable and scalable while maintaining acceptable levels of technical debt and risk. 
 
Security 
The Security function protects our people, premises, and digital systems with the objective of 
maintaining trust in National Grid services, focusing on: 
• 
Reduction in likelihood and impact of security incidents 
• 
Compliance with relevant laws, standards and regulations (e.g., NERC, PCI DSS, 
GDPR, NIS-R) 
• 
Improved user experience and standard of security practices across National Grid 
 
The Security function aims to reduce the likelihood and impact of physical and cyber security 
incidents affecting National Grid. It does this by championing security best practices, technology, 
and promoting a security-awareness culture.  
 
Other Category 
For accounting purposes, there is an additional category listed in Attachment 2 to this report.   The 
“Other” category has 3 main elements: 
• 
The “IT4IT” sub-category acts as a funding bucket for NPV-positive projects to 
enable efficiency savings in our IT-run business operations.   
• 
The “Other” sub-category is the allocation of operating expense overheads such as 
Enterprise Architecture and Solution Delivery charges to a centralized account.   
The capital charges for this overhead are made directly to individual projects.    
• 
Finally, “Burdens” are the net removal of operating expense burdens to ensure our 
reporting agrees with our Corporate Controllable Cost reporting.  Operating 
expense burdens are consolidated and reported separately under non-controllable 
costs in our corporate reporting packs. 
 
For FY23 and FY24 there are Rhode Island separation costs flowing through this category.  
National Grid is currently providing IT services (applications, infrastructure, networks, etc..) to 
PPL as part of a 2-year Transition Services Agreement (TSA) following the sale of the RI Gas and 
Electric business.  Significant effort is required to manage and track an orderly exit of all IT TSA 
services.  National Grid must provide subject matter expertise, migrate critical application data, 
design and implement interim state processes and remove any customizations introduced to 
support delivery of the TSA.   The costs for this are recovered from PPL and do not impact New 
York rate payers.   The Group Functions portfolio is responsible for managing the expenditure 
although the costs role up through the “Other Category”.

Delivery
Progress on delivery continues although slightly behind 
expectations.   Significant releases this quarter include:  
Advanced Distribution Management Systems up feeders, 
Advanced Metering Infrastructure minimum viable product

data analytics tool to detect non-compliance.
Challenges
Commercial and contracting issues and chip shortages still 
exist in the post-COVID era which is slowing spend and 
creating challenges.   Specialist IT resources and business 
resources are proving difficult to secure. However, capabilities 
are being delivered across the portfolios and management is 
actively re-prioritizing resources to deliver for customers.   
Financial Performance 
Financial performance is close to budget. The ‘Other’ category 
is offsetting the underspend in the Electric and Security 
portfolios, with a $23m budget phasing adjustment (following 
refinement of business plans) plus a reallocation of funds to 
Gas and Customer to meet user demands.
The remaining overspend in the “Other” category is the 
transition services agreement to PPL following the RI sale. The 
agreement ensures an orderly exit of all IT TSA services which 
National Grid is providing to cover subject matter expertise, 
migrate critical application data, design, implement interim state 
processes and remove customizations.   
Although this is being managed through the Group Functions 
portfolio there is no impact to NY customers.   Forecast for 
these costs is estimated at ~$22m which explains the 
forecasted overspend on budget across IT.

• The Customer portfolio remains on track to meet
additional demand ($11.3M) from the business over
the initial plan.
•
Reallocation of funding across IT has been identified with
demand for services remaining steady from Q2 to Q3;
•
Unified Web Portal 2.0 – significant driver of the year to
date increase over budget.   Additional spend will provide
an improved user experience.
•
Technical Debt – Targeting technical debt remediations
that support the Customer System and the Customer
offices.
• Major releases in Q3 included:
•
Deployed Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI)
Customer Portal update (My Energy Usage widget),
allowing for MVP customers to see energy use within a
specified period of time .
•
Implemented (5) Tactical ZBR Interactive Voice Response
(IVR) improvements forecasting a savings of $225K/month.
This brings the annualized total of IVR efficiency
improvements to $10M.
•
Successfully implemented the 2nd release of “Traintrax”
which provides system analysts improved system
management of CSS batch process.
•
CSS Preferred Name, GBE Preferred Pronoun and GBE
Preferred Name was successfully implemented into
production to comply with the Preferred Name/Pronoun
legislation passed in New York State.
•
Deployed (2) Bulk Pay change features into UWP
production environment to improve Customer satisfaction.
•
Delivered critical Clean Energy update to Customer
account validation service application, which is used by
trade allies and vendors that provide services to NY
customers.

Portfolio Commentary
Group Functions is tracking to budget for full year forecast with 
accelerated run rate in Q4. YTD financial results are lagging 
to forecast due to delays in project start-ups.
Key Solutions Delivered in Q3:
Core PowerPlan Upgrade & Lease Consolidation
The upgrade allows us to decommission a 
standalone PowerPlan instance for Lease as well as to 
eliminate tech debt by bringing the application and underlying 
infrastructure to supported versions. Decreases the complexity 
of future upgrades reducing cost to maintain the application 
and ensures continued compliance of this critical SOX 
application.
Procure to Pay (P2P) Data Analysis Tool (Palantir)
Enhancements delivering advanced analytics on 
fraudulent activities by connecting to all the systems 
generating P2P transactions to enable 100% compliance. 
Enables auto alerts & outcome tracking on non-
compliant activity, direct triage email capability from Foundry 
and trend reporting based on Detection Strategies.
HR Support Pack Upgrade (Q3 Release)
Delivers the Federal and State required updates for Payroll 
and Tax compliance and to comply with regulatory reporting.
Onboarding 2.0
Brings improved productivity for new hires by enhancing user 
interfaces and utilizing auto-population. Contributes to 
reducing days to onboard new resources for equipment 
and access provisioning.

National Grid 
DPIT
Financial Performance
• Financials: Year to date ~$14M favorable to budget
driven by budget phasing across the portfolio.
• The change in full year forecast since Q2 due to increased
scope for Digital Workplace Services. DPIT is balancing
spend within the portfolio and forecasting to FY23 budget,
with:
• Slight Capex overspend driven by Data Center
Transformation due to increased upfront cost to drive
additional downstream operational savings, and Supply
Chain issues causing delays in the schedule
• Opex underspend due to costs shifting out of DPIT to
NG exceptional funding
• Technical Debt: Overall reduced to 16.9% (FY23 goal:
18%)
• Benefit to Customers delivered through Q3:
• Unified Technology Operations Center(UTOC) Minimum
Viable Product to provide overwatch on all technology
and provide predictive analysis of asset health for
proactive maintenance – ticketing solution is 100% live
• Network and CNI upgrades to maintain reliability,
availability and improve security
• Windows as a Service deployed updates to >23K
devices
• Cloud & Hosting: migration of data ~ 98% complete to
reduce risk of applications hosted on old
and unsupported hardware, reduce Technical debt, and
enable Data Center Transformation
• Digital Platforms: several deliverables to provide secure
/reliable/scalable/modernization improvements

Information Technology Capital Investment Report for 
Quarter Ended March 31, 2023 
I.
Introduction
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submit this Information Technology (“IT”) Capital Investment Quarterly Report 
(“IT Quarterly Report”) for the fourth quarter (Q4) of fiscal year 2023 (“FY23”).1  Pursuant to the 
Public Service Commission’s (“Commission”) January 20, 2022 Order in Cases 20-E-0380 and 
20-G-0381, and August 12, 2021 Order in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-0310, the Company is to
provide quarterly variance reports to Department of Public Service Staff (“Staff”) regarding IT
capital projects and investments.2  The IT Quarterly Report provides an explanation of the
Company’s overall IT investment plan approach, descriptions of program investment categories,
and a comparison of budgeted to actual spending.
IT capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s operating 
companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. (“Service 
Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara Mohawk, 
KEDNY, and KEDLI, in the form of Service Company rent expense once the investments are in-
service.  The Service Company rent expense includes a return on the capital investment (net of 
deferred taxes) plus booked depreciation expense. 
Through Q4 FY23, National Grid spent $367.1 million compared to a year-to-date Service 
Company budget of $341.0 million, representing a $26.1 million overspend.  Attachment 1 
includes detail on budgets and actual spending for each of the portfolios and commentary regarding 
performance which has been presented to each of the Chief Information Officers responsible for 
the respective portfolios.  
Attachment 2 includes a detailed breakdown of individual project spend by portfolio compared to 
the budgeted spend for each of those investments. 
II.
Program Categories/Spending Rationales
National Grid has organized the US Information Technology organization into six areas:

IT capital investment is tracked based on these area designations. Descriptions of each portfolio 
category/spending rationale are provided below. 
Group Functions  
Group Functions executes National Grid’s digital roadmaps, leveraging technology and 
reimagining processes in support of Finance, Enterprise Business Services, Human Resources, 
Legal, and Safety Health & Environmental, continuing to upgrade SOX related systems, and 
retiring outdated systems. 
United States Electric 
Provides IT Support to our US Electric Distribution and Transmission businesses.  The group’s 
primary focus is modernizing our key legacy operational systems while building capabilities that 
will enable the energy transition and transformation to a Distribution System Operator (DSO).   
Through digital delivery, the United State Electric organization provides greater efficiency and 
data driven insights into our workforce operations that provide:  

More automated and reliable grid controls systems

Capital programs and projects that support the proliferation of Distributed Energy
Resources (DERs)

A growing market of prosumer electric customers
United States Gas 
Provides IT Support to our US Gas Distribution and Transmission businesses by developing digital 
products that deliver continuous improvement of our asset lifecycle management capabilities 
through:   

Risk-based asset investment planning

Performance-based maintenance

AI-based work optimization

Mobile field products
Customer 
Provides IT Support to our US Customer business, delivering best-in-class digital products that 
increase engagement and reduce costs to serve by:  

Modernizing our legacy “back-end” IT estate to support more digital products

Liberating data and creating an abstracted and real-time customer data platform to assist
with achieving energy efficiency targets
Exhibit ___ (ITDP-2R)

--- Page 267 ---
Page 3 of 5 
Digital Platforms and Infrastructure Technology (DPIT) (Formerly Infrastructure and Operations) 
Supports our internal IT Architecture covering Cloud and Hosting, Critical Network Infrastructure, 
Networks, End User Experience and Operations.  DPIT is focused on reducing National Grid’s 
technical debt through cost effective, modernized IT infrastructure, enabling cloud capabilities that 
meet our risk profile.   The organization enables a connected, seamless enterprise that is flexible, 
secure, reliable and scalable while maintaining acceptable levels of technical debt and risk. 
Security 
The Security function protects our people, premises, and digital systems with the objective of 
maintaining trust in National Grid services, focusing on: 
•
Reduction in likelihood and impact of security incidents
•
Compliance with relevant laws, standards and regulations (e.g., NERC, PCI DSS,
GDPR, NIS-R)
•
Improved user experience and standard of security practices across National Grid
The Security function aims to reduce the likelihood and impact of physical and cyber security 
incidents affecting National Grid. It does this by championing security best practices, adopting 
technology advancements, and promoting a security-awareness culture. 
Other Category 
For accounting purposes, there is an additional category listed in Attachment 2 to this report.   The 
“Other” category has 3 main elements: 
•
The “IT4IT” sub-category acts as a funding bucket for NPV-positive projects to
enable efficiency savings in our IT-run business operations.
•
The “Other” sub-category is the allocation of operating expense overheads such as
Enterprise Architecture and Solution Delivery charges to a centralized account.
The capital charges for this overhead are made directly to individual projects.
•
“Burdens” are the net removal of operating expense burdens to ensure our
reporting agrees with our Corporate Controllable Cost reporting.  Operating
expense burdens are consolidated and reported separately under non-controllable
costs in our corporate reporting packs.
Following the sale of the Rhode Island Gas and Electric business to PPL, associated separation 
costs are and will flow through this category in FY23 and FY24.  National Grid is currently 
providing IT services (applications, infrastructure, networks, etc..) to PPL as part of a 2-year 
Transition Services Agreement (TSA) following the sale.  Significant effort is required to manage 
and track an orderly exit of all IT TSA services.  National Grid must provide subject matter 
expertise, migrate critical application data, design and implement interim state processes, and 
remove any customizations introduced to support delivery of the TSA.   The costs for this are 
recovered from PPL and do not impact New York rate payers.   The Group Functions portfolio is 
responsible for managing the expenditure but the costs role up through the “Other Category”. 
The summaries below explain the subjects presented in the attachments to the Q4 FY23 report.

Financial Performance
With the exception of the variance in the “Other” category, portfolio performance is very close to budget.
Throughout the year there has been reprioritization of expenditure, including in the Gas portfolio to deliver
Continued Scaling and Evolution, to shift focus to projects as needed. Group Functions required additional
resources to integrate applications in Procure to Pay, Customer continues to develop the unified web portal,
and DPIT capitalized software following a review of accounting policies, all of which drove budget variances.
These were offset by the Electric and Security portfolios, each of which reprioritized work based on demand
and resources.
The ‘Other’ category includes the transition services agreement to PPL following the RI sale. The agreement
ensures an orderly exit of all IT TSA services which National Grid is providing to cover subject matter
expertise, migrate critical application data, design, implement interim state processes and remove
customizations.
Although this is being managed through the Group Functions portfolio, there is no impact
to NY customers and they will not be charged for ~$20m of RI spend that is the main driver of the overall
budget variance.

9
National Grid 
US Electric
Financial Performance
Variance Drivers
• Full year under-spend of $22M CAPEX and $1.6M OPEX is 
being driven by supply chain delays, resource constraints, and 
various deliverability constraints that delayed the start of 
planned products. There was also a $4.8m underspend due to 
scope reduction for Vegetation Management Optimization as it 
was determined this scope would not provide sufficient 
customer value.
Major Releases
• Field Collections System (FCS) Upgrade: Remediated Tech 
Debt by upgrading our FCS system to its latest supportable 
version on October 28th. This system acts as our centralized 
billing hub for our Residential Customers by collecting, 
organizing, processing and distributing various data points to 
our critical billing systems (CSS, CRS) 
• MV90 Upgrade: Successfully completed on November 11th, 
making our US Electric Meter Reading System more reliable 
and secure for our Commercial and Industrial Customers; this 
system supports 40% of US Electric Revenue 
• FutureNow: Transformation Product released to the 
Transmission Business on November 7th, marking the 
completion of a key milestone in ensuring that the ~$22.6M in 
Forecasted US Type 1 Benefits are successfully delivered 
through FY24.
• Corporate PI (Process Intelligence): Went live on 3/28, 
allowing quicker and more reliable access to SCADA Data for 
end-users outside CNI to facilitate planning and analytics of 
load demand and supply

Portfolio Commentary
Variance Drivers
•
Reallocation of funding across IT to meet customer 
demand with Unified Web Portal 2.0 – a significant driver 
of the increase over budget.   The additional spend will 
provide an improved user experience.
•
Technical Debt – Targeting technical debt remediations 
that support the Customer System and the Customer 
offices contributed to the reallocation of costs over initial 
budget.
• Major Releases:
•
Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI). Released 
several features to support rapid installation of additional 
AMI meters and handling billing exceptions
•
My Business Account (MBA). Achieved 36% FY23 
Product Adoption, delivering $2M in FYTD cost savings, 
66% above target. Releases include: (1) CRIS Paperless 
Billing capability, enabling customers to easily bulk 
enroll/de-enroll in Paperless Billing; (2) Ability to view 
Account Contact Information to more easily identify 
accounts; (3) MuleSoft Platform email capability to 
proactively alert any API issues before widespread 
customer impact.
•
Call Center Technologies. completed Startek (3rd party 
vendor managing customer calls) onboarding, which will 
manage a portion of call center activity (50% anticipated in 
future state); benefits include increased customer 
satisfaction and cost savings due to competitive bid 
process. Completed consolidation of data centers, which 
reduced RTB costs by $72k annually

record management capabilities for easier and faster access 
to system data and tools to better manage user requests.
Workforce Data Domain

data drives accuracy and compliance. Minimizes cost and 
friction by reducing data defects, fewer manual interventions 
for data quality checks and maintenance of integrations.
SAP PI to PO Upgrade – Release 2
Migrated 36 interfaces to the new PO platform to ensure we 
are meeting the latest encryption security standard.
RPA Manual Journal Entries
Reduces risk and streamlines process in reduction of manual 
journal entry tracking and consolidation of journal data 
sources while improving the employee experience.
Digitizing Learning Global Support Model
Drives streamlining & operational excellence towards Global 
Learning Management Services.

23
National Grid 
Mobilization Summary - FY24
Key Outcomes to be Achieved in FY24
•
Asset Health - Migrate 101 interfaces from PI to PO to mitigate security risks and ensure latest 
encryption standards are met.
•
Join to Leave - People Digital Transformation - Focus on Core, Data and Processes, revert 
MyHub to standard, enabling People Function Target Operating Model. This is intended to drive 
Operational Efficiency, User Experience focussed on Self Service, leading to improved Data 
Quality and Compliance.
•
Record to Report - Increased standardization and automation in reporting. Automate data feeds 
and leverage Wdesk to reduce use of offline files. Continue to reduce manual effort associated 
with journal entries via RPA and Blackline integration.
•
Source to Pay - Implement Ariba Guided Buying across US (NY and NE) enabling 
intelligent cataloge search resulting in increased electronic purchasing, reducing free text po’s, 
and increasing electronic invoicing. Implement next phase of Ariba and upon completion enable 
retiring SAP SRM system.
•
Plan to Perform - Implement three separate product releases to lessen the dependency on offline 
financial models by automating calculations. Will enable collaborative working in connected 
data environments which will reduce the planning cycle from 15 to 3 weeks, thereby releasing 
resource effort to focus on other priorities.

Project Delivery - Initial scope delivered

Lessons Learned?

Allocation 
Code
4481
US MDS-Wholesale Settlement System 
Replacement
   4,805,900          316,300 
   5,122,200 Using a fix price contract where feasible and practical should be used as appropriate to reduce risks to the 
project.
“Collaboratively developed software” as in this case, requires Senior Subject Matter Expert (SME) Interface 
resources during coding and implementation due to the maiden development of the IEE Settlement 
application.
Given this software was not “an off the shelf solution”, agile delivery over the applied waterfall delivery would
have identified the significance of interface design errors causing delivery delays.
This investment will have a positive impact on the ability to complete the daily settlement and
reconciliation process, as the automation of the load data will mitigate the risk of manual error and
shorten the time required to complete the tasks associated with the process.
l By consolidating the two platforms into a vender supported application we will insure a disaster
recovery plan that is site tested for the NY Wholesale Energy Settlement Market and improve
performance.
l Stability and availability of a key business critical application.
l Elimination of manual data transfers from the MV-90 xi system.
l Eliminate manual comparisons and aggregation calculations between the respective ISO’s data and
National Grids data.
541T
4483
US Control-Transmission Outage 
Application (iTOA) Upgrade
   4,158,000 
   550,000 
   4,708,000 The new and improved Integrated Outage Application delivered a new web application platform, improved 
user access, and increased application stability in a new and supported environment. From a business 
perspective, it was unclear what the full breadth of expectations were. What were the responsibilities of the 
business roles - It took a long time for the business to catch up with what was going on within IT Tools and 
delivery methodologies (Sprints and Iterations).
This investment will ensure the continued ability to track electric transmission and distribution outages, both
planned and unplanned, allowing the control rooms to share information with the field and other required
third parties. This will assist in running the electric network safely and meeting National Grid's regulatory
requirements.
The new web-based technology and components of the application will allow for easier sharing
of information and ensure continued support, reliability, and security. This will provide National Grid with the
future ability to connect directly with other Local Control Centres in the region who also use or will use the

5841c
401(k) Administration Changes
            836,000             80,000             916,000 Lesson 1: Scope Management – What we could do better:
The connectivity testing with the external vendor did not consider exact steps during Testing as it would be in 
Production. The Test setup was different than in Production and the Testing team was not aware of this. As a 
result, the connectivity failed during go-live. We had taken next 30 days to set it up correctly and test again. 
All 30 days the files were exchanged manually.
Recommendation: It is important to ensure that Test environment is setup exactly as in Production and THEN 
verify it.
Lesson 2: Business Case & Benefits Management – What we did right
The team discovered a complex defect during user acceptance testing. The defect, which was not related to 
the changes made by the project, was subsequently fixed by the team. By fixing the issue we made sure the 
promised business benefits were not compromised. The team was able to discover a complex issue outside of 
the scope and resolve it as part of the delivery. 
Recommendation: Always look at a long term benefit for the overall product, not just what is in scope for an 
individual project.
Benefits the Company and participants will reap by the implementation of the approved plan design 
changes: 
1. Plans Consolidation: Merging the two 401(k) Plans into one will simplify and provide efficiencies in 
plan administration for both National Grid and Vanguard, and in return, Vanguard has offered to pass 
those savings onto participants. This equates to participant savings of 30% year over year. 
 Streamlines participant data transfer process with employee job transfers (union to 
management and vice versa) and eliminates manual process by Vanguard and improves 
efficiency through automation. 
 The Summary Plan Description is combined to one master document using appendices for 
match formulas for each employee grouping. 
 The weekly inbound participant election file will be combined to one file. 
 Eliminates the need for a Master Trust on the stable value fund and required filings for the 
Master Trust. 
 Labor efforts for Compliance and mandatory filings will reduce costs. Elimination of one Plan 
audit, two form 5500s (one plan and the stable value Master Trust) and one financial 
statement. Thereby reduces auditing, financial statement compilation and tax preparation 
costs by approximately $35,000 per year. 
 Non-Discrimination Testing is conducted on one Plan and reducing the chance of plan failure. 
 Vanguard adhoc reporting becomes more efficient and timelier. 
2. New Features: The Roth 401(k) is a feature that has several potential benefits. The Roth 401
(k) was first introduced in 2006 and has grown in popularity since then. Currently, 74% of Vanguard 
clients offer the Roth 401(k) feature. Adding this feature provides employees with another way to 
save for retirement within the 401(k) plans in a tax-friendly way, allowing participants to prepare 
better for retirement and taxes they will have to pay in retirement. It also provides new hires into the 
Company who have a Roth 401(k) at another employer the ability to move their Roth 401(k) savings 
into the National Grid 401(k) plans. This feature is not currently an option, causing some concern 
among new hires. The Services Delivery Center consistently receives inquiries from new hires if a 
Roth 401(k) is available allowing them to rollover money from previous employers. Adding the Roth 
401(k) feature to the NaƟonal Grid 401(k) plans is another step in meeƟng the needs of our mulƟ generaƟonal workforce and keeping

Information Technology & Digital Capital Investment Report for  
Quarter Ended June 30, 2023 
I.
Introduction
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submit this Information Technology & Digital (“IT&D”) Capital Investment 
Quarterly Report (“IT&D Quarterly Report”) for the first quarter (Q1) of fiscal year 2024 
(“FY24”).1  Pursuant to the Public Service Commission’s (“Commission”) January 20, 2022 Order 
in Cases 20-E-0380 and 20-G-0381, and August 12, 2021 Order in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-
0310, the Company is to provide quarterly variance reports to Department of Public Service Staff 
(“Staff”) regarding IT&D capital projects and investments.2  The IT&D Quarterly Report provides 
an explanation of the Company’s overall IT&D investment plan approach, descriptions of program 
investment categories, and a comparison of budgeted to actual spending. 
IT&D capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s 
operating companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. 
(“Service Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara 
Mohawk, KEDNY, and KEDLI, in the form of Service Company rent expense once the 
investments are in-service.  The Service Company rent expense includes a return on the capital 
investment (net of deferred taxes) plus booked depreciation expense. 
Through Q1 FY24, National Grid spent $75.7 million compared to a year-to-date Service 
Company budget of $67.3 million, representing an $8.4 million overspend.  Attachment 1 includes 
detail on budgets and actual spending for each of the portfolios and commentary regarding 
performance which has been presented to each of the Chief Information and Digital Officers 
(“CIDOs”)  responsible for their respective portfolios.  
Attachment 2 includes a detailed breakdown of individual project spend by portfolio compared to 
the budgeted spend for each of those investments. 
II.
Program Categories/Spending Rationales
National Grid has organized the US Information & Digital Technology organization into six areas:

IT&D capital investment is tracked based on these area designations. Descriptions of each

Group Functions  
Group Functions executes National Grid’s digital roadmaps, leveraging technology and 
reimagining processes in support of Finance, Enterprise Business Services, Human Resources, 
Legal, and Safety Health & Environmental, continuing to upgrade SOX related systems, and 
retiring outdated systems. 
United States Electric 
Provides IT&D support to our US Electric Distribution and Transmission businesses.  The group’s 
primary focus is modernizing our key legacy operational systems while building capabilities that 
will enable the energy transition and transformation to a Distribution System Operator (DSO).   
Through digital delivery, the United State Electric organization provides greater efficiency and 
data driven insights into our workforce operations that provide:  

More automated and reliable grid controls systems

Capital programs and projects that support the proliferation of Distributed Energy
Resources (DERs)

A growing market of prosumer electric customers
United States Gas 
Provides IT&D Support to our US Gas Distribution and Transmission businesses by developing 
digital products that deliver continuous improvement of our asset lifecycle management 
capabilities through:   

Risk-based asset investment planning

Performance-based maintenance

AI-based work optimization

Mobile field products
Customer

increase engagement and reduce costs to serve by:  

Modernizing our legacy “back-end” IT&D systems to support more digital products

Liberating data and creating an abstracted and real-time customer data platform to assist
with achieving energy efficiency targets

Digital Platforms and Infrastructure Technology (DPIT) 
Supports our internal IT&D Architecture covering Cloud and Hosting, Critical Network 
Infrastructure, Networks, End User Experience and Operations.  DPIT is focused on reducing 
National Grid’s technical debt through cost effective, modernized IT&D infrastructure, enabling 
cloud capabilities that meet our risk profile.   The organization enables a connected, seamless 
enterprise that is flexible, secure, reliable and scalable while maintaining acceptable levels of 
technical debt and risk. 
Security 
The Security function protects our people, premises, and digital systems with the objective of 
maintaining trust in National Grid services, focusing on: 
•
Reduction in likelihood and impact of security incidents
•
Compliance with relevant laws, standards and regulations (e.g., NERC, PCI DSS,
GDPR, NIS-R)
•
Improved user experience and standard of security practices across National Grid
The Security function aims to reduce the likelihood and impact of physical and cyber security 
incidents affecting National Grid. It does this by championing security best practices, adopting 
technology advancements, and promoting a security-awareness culture. 
Other Category 
For accounting purposes, there is an additional category listed in Attachment 2 to this report.   The 
“Other” category has 4 main elements: 
•
The “IT4IT” sub-category acts as a funding bucket for NPV-positive projects to
enable efficiency savings in our IT&D-run business operations.
•
The “Other” sub-category is the allocation of operating expense overheads such as
Enterprise Architecture and Solution Delivery charges to a centralized account.
The capital charges for this overhead are made directly to individual projects.
•
“Burdens” are the net removal of operating expense burdens to ensure our
reporting agrees with our Corporate Controllable Cost reporting.  Operating
expense burdens are consolidated and reported separately under non-controllable
costs in our corporate reporting packs.
•
“RI Sale”; following the sale of the Rhode Island Gas and Electric business to PPL,
associated separation costs flow through this category.  National Grid is currently
providing IT&D services (applications, infrastructure, networks, etc.) to PPL as
part of a 2-year Transition Services Agreement (TSA) following the sale.
Significant effort is required to manage and track an orderly exit of all IT&D TSA
services.  National Grid must provide subject matter expertise, migrate critical
application data, design and implement interim state processes, and remove any
customizations introduced to support delivery of the TSA.   The costs for this are
recovered from PPL and do not impact New York rate payers.  The Group
Functions portfolio is responsible for managing the expenditure but the costs role
up through the “Other Category”.

the portfolio.  Each bar is color-coded to give an overview of the comparative 
spend per program.  
c. The third page of each portfolio section provides a status update on the various 
projects.  A priority investments list for the portfolio and their status appears at 
the top right hand of the page. Blue means complete, green means on track, 
amber means some risk, and red means focused intervention required.

the IT&D leadership team.

Q1 Releases
• By transitioning to an agile approach, the company has made
some impactful releases across the IT&D portfolio this quarter:
• Continued Scaling & Evolution (CS&E) has released a
document management system to over 1,000 Downstate
NY users.
• Customer has improved contact center technology to be
compliant with FCC mandates and improving
functionality and resiliency to around 2,000 users.
• Ariba release in May impacts 1,400 suppliers enhancing
e-invoicing capabilities and catalog coverage.
Challenges
• Business engagement and customer input is undergoing a
learning experience as we transition to agile delivery.
• Cost pressures and resource challenges are being managed
across the portfolio.
Financial Performance 
• Year to Date financial performance is tracking close to budget
once accounting adjustments are corrected and RI costs
excluded.   There was an accrual duplication of $7.1m in CS&E
which is  partially offset by intercompany credits of $2.6m for
eHub and $1.1m for MyHub.
• The full year forecast overage is driven by separation activities
for RI which will not impact NY customers.
• Note: a Construction Overhead Accounting adjustment has
been made to correct an FY23 miss-allocation to individual
projects.   For FY24 this means individual portfolios received
unexpected credits or debits.   The net impact is zero across
IT&D but it does present challenges in individual portfolios.
This is though being managed across the organization.

Q1 Releases
• CS&E – Tesco Meter Management system went live on

traceability of the status of the meters from the time of
receipt at the shop to the time they are either retired or
installed at customer's site. Deployed Docuware

Portfolio Commentary
Financials
YTD Totex actuals vs budget variance ($2.2M)  mainly driven by 
•
Construction Overhead charges of ~1M Capex to multiple initiatives, creating 
an unplanned spend spike 
•
Generation Asset Management – walked in at the reduction of existing 
initiatives without re-forecasting to include $1.03M within Q1
•
FutureNow – overrun of $800K Capex 
•
Shift to right for IDS Replacement and Demand Planning & Track and Trace 
initiatives, causing underspends to date
Q1 Releases
Core / Digital:
•
FutureNow: Forecasting 2.0 MVP (financial forecast entry tool to flow project
financials into Copperleaf) implemented. Forecasting now lives within One Integrated 
Plan and replaces the PowerBI forecast file. In the first 3 weeks about 
134 Forecasters updated 1211 projects using this tool that improves user experience 
and reduces time required to complete Forecasting.​
•
Veg+: recently deployed ViperPro Workflow for Electric Transmission, building on 
the previous release for Distribution, which enables optimization of vegetation 
management through the advanced digital tool (ViperPro) providing whole 
cost vegetation management control and optimization​
•
NYISO PMU Large Generators initiative was completed, bringing NG in 
compliance with the NYISO mandate to support 3rd party Phasor Measurement Unit
(PMU) data transmission to NYISO, and addressing technical debt.
Strategic: 
•
DERA+: successfully completed a production release which includes our initial
commitment of Operate "Most Valuable Features" - Making operating DER 
aggregations and their associated DERs on our networks safe and reliable​ - Achieve 
80% coverage of key operational features required by the control center(s) for DER 
aggregation operations.​ 2. Delivered initial features to handle resubmitted 
applications (earlier than expected)​
•
GridMod TOMS: Integrated system and user functionality to support
GIS/Snowflake/Mulesoft integration into TOMS on weekly basis including circuit 
information data updates as well as 4RF NMS interface integration and data loading
•
GridMod Cyber Security: Strategic Privileged Access Management (PAM) tool
delivered to manage, track and enhance the security of privileged accounts across 
the US CNI environment for ADMS​
•
GridMod Data Management: Loaded PI Tag data from Corporate PI into 
Snowflake to enable users to search PI data based on assets, circuit names,
substation names and geographical locations. Migrated P6 historical data from 
PostgreSQL legacy database
into Snowflake and built generic views for project, 
activity, and resource, so that the Capital Delivery Team can meet all their analytical
needs. Continue to build "One system One Model" to improve data access and 
analytics capabilities

Portfolio Commentary
Financials
•
The majority of the year-to-date variance is made of accounting
adjustments - $2.6m credit for E-hub and $1.1m credit for MyHub
for a missed accrual, both related to inter-company adjustments.
An additional $1.1m was the COH adjustment credit.
•
Full year forecast variance is due to scope and cost pressures
across the portfolio.
Q1 – Successes and Go-Lives
•
R2R: Reduction of manual journals through business adoption of RPA
for prep, park and post of regulatory deferrals and pension journals (3%).
Deployed 12 US GAAP templates for statutory reporting within Wdesk.
Use of standardized templates will reduce cycle times and minimize
manual preparation and risk of error.
•
S2P - Ariba: Release 1 Go-Live in May 2023, enabled 1,400 suppliers,
11 buying channels, and 48 catalogs to continue to increase e-invoicing
and catalog coverage. Ariba Release 2 sanction paper to be submitted
imminently and will automate accruals in Ariba to further reduce manual 
journal entries and complete the exit from SRM for all procurement 
activities. Completed F&A for Planning Repository and are recommending
replacing Quickbase with Planview, the team is working to build out the
business case and sanction paper with a target kickoff in Q3 
for Quickbase implementation.
•
J2L: Sodales Union Job Bidding solution digitizing paper-based process
for union job bidding successfully rolled out to all US jurisdiction recruiters
and hiring managers (~950). Payroll - Cost Center & Time Reporting data 
quality improvement of ~30% by remediating data sync issues (R1 May 
2023).
•
PLTP: Implementation has commenced. First phase of go-live for Group 
functions Opex in October. Architectural agreement on the use of
Snowflake has been achieved.
•
SEA: Launched initiative for a global Incident Management and reporting 
product/platform (Cority). Commencing execution in August and once fully 
launched, will reduce NG RTB by ~$200k.

Key Outcomes to be Achieved in FY24
•
Asset Health - Migrate 101 interfaces from PI to PO to mitigate security risks and ensure latest
encryption standards are met.
•
Join to Leave - People Digital Transformation - Focus on Core, Data and Processes, revert MyHub to
standard, enabling People Function Target Operating Model. This is intended to drive Operational
Efficiency, User Experience focussed on Self Service, leading to improved Data Quality and
Compliance.
•
Record to Report - Increased standardization and automation in reporting. Automate data feeds and
leverage Wdesk to reduce use of offline files. Continue to reduce manual effort associated with journal 
entries via RPA and Blackline integration.
•
Source to Pay - Implement Ariba Guided Buying across US (NY and NE) enabling
intelligent catalog search resulting in increased electronic purchasing, reducing free text po’s,
and increasing electronic invoicing. Implement next phase of Ariba and upon completion enable retiring
SAP SRM system.
•
Plan to Perform - Implement three separate product releases to lessen the dependency on offline
financial models by automating calculations. Will enable collaborative working in connected
data environments which will reduce the planning cycle from 15 to 3 weeks, thereby releasing resource
effort to focus on other priorities.

•

support Optel circuit replacements
•

performed on our assets

Fiscal Year 2022 Information Technology 
Capital Investment Plan 
 
I. 
Introduction 
 
Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (Niagara Mohawk), The Brooklyn Union Gas Company 
(KEDNY), and KeySpan Gas East Corporation (KEDLI) (together “National Grid” or the 
“Companies”) submits its Information Technology (“IT”) Capital Investment Plan (the 
“Investment Plan”) for fiscal year 2023 (“FY23 Plan”).1  This submission is in compliance with 
Section IV.6.5 of the Joint Proposal adopted by the New York Public Service Commission (“PSC” 
or the “Commission”) January 20, 2022 in Cases 20-E-0380 and 20-G-0381, and Section IV.10.5 
of the Joint Proposal adopted by the Commission August 12, 2021 in Cases 19-G-0309 and 19-G-
0310.2 
 
IT capital projects and investments that are shared investments across National Grid’s operating 
companies are implemented and owned by National Grid USA Service Company, Inc. (“Service 
Company”) and allocated to the benefiting US operating companies, including Niagara Mohawk, 
KEDNY and KEDLI in the form of an annual rent expense once the investments are in-service.  
The rent expense includes a return on the capital investment plus depreciation expense.   
 
The FY23 Plan is made up of in-flight projects that will require capital spending to complete as 
well as projects that will be sanctioned and begin to incur capital charges during the fiscal year.  
In total, the FY23 Plan reflects Service Company capital expenditures of $299.257 million across 
the US operating companies.  Of this amount, approximately $288.894 million is for projects that 
benefit and, therefore, are chargeable to Niagara Mohawk, $228.342 million to KEDNY and 
$227.365 million to KEDLI.3  The FY23 Plan provided in Attachment 1 includes a list of projects, 
forecast in-service dates, and the allocators used to determine the rent expense for the operating 
companies that will benefit from each project, along with FY23 Service Company IT capital costs 
and the full Service Company project spend expected for each investment.   
 
National Grid’s IT organization continuously reviews the Plan relative to current business 
requirements, risks and information.  The FY23 Plan assumes that the impacts of the novel 
coronavirus (COVID–19) pandemic or any impacts from the conflict in Ukraine will not

II. 
Development of the Capital Plan 
 
To determine projects for inclusion in the FY23 Plan, National Grid engaged in an iterative process 
that involved collaboration with Jurisdictional representatives and the functional business areas 
(e.g., Operations, Customer and Digital, Network Strategy, and Finance and Shared Services) to 
identify the investments of highest priority for inclusion in the Plan.  This process was aligned to 
the corporate budgeting process and strategic portfolio reviews.  
  
The development of the FY23 Plan (portfolio reviews) was based on an assessment and analysis 
of current and proposed programs aligned to the Company’s IT strategic focus - build and maintain 
the foundation, drive new capabilities, and enable cost savings.  We reviewed each program and 
balanced funding across focus areas to optimize investments and drive value.  The FY23 portfolio 
is focused on the following: 
 
 Fulfilling regulatory and legal mandates 
 Reducing cyber and operational risk  
 Driving standardization and modernization 
 Building tools and platforms to empower our people 
 Safeguarding critical business applications 
 Building new capabilities for improved business performance  
 Implementing cost efficiencies and saving programs to achieve year-over-year run-the-
business (“RTB”) cost reductions 
 
In building the FY23 Plan, National Grid first identified the amount of work remaining and the 
delivery timeline for in-flight, multi-year investments.  Next, new investments to address 
compliance with a legal or regulatory requirement/mandate or an open corporate risk were added 
to the Plan.  Third, investments that focused on IT infrastructure – primarily investments to 
upgrade/replace/add functionality that would create reliability in systems and fix foundational 
capabilities necessary for operations and/or future aspirations of the business (including ensuring 
digital security) were included.  Finally, the IT team worked closely with the Jurisdiction and 
business executive sponsors to focus on their top project requests.   
 
After this analysis, IT distributed a draft investment plan to business functions, Jurisdictional 
representatives, and other key stakeholders for feedback and held review sessions on the proposed 
plan.  A final Investment Plan review occurs each fiscal year with the Jurisdictional Presidents, 
Jurisdictional delegates, and functional executives.  Upon the review and approval of the 
Investment Plan by the Jurisdictional Presidents and functional executives, the consolidated 
financial information from the Plan, by jurisdiction and company, is incorporated with the IT 
O&M requirements into the IT budget.  The IT budget is then reviewed and approved by the New 
York Chief Information Officer (“CIO”), Global CIO, and Corporate Finance, and is incorporated 
into a consolidated National Grid USA budget for approval by the National Grid plc Board.
